company_description: Uses machine-learning models to identify and develop deposits of copper, lithium, nickel, and cobalt globally. Flagship project is the Mingomba copper deposit in Zambia; the company exists at the intersection of AI-driven exploration software and traditional mining operations.
lead_investors: Durable Capital Partners, T. Rowe Price
co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, BOND, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Earthshot VC, Equinor, July Fund, Mitsubishi, Standard Investments, StepStone Group, WCM Investment Management
robotnik_take: $537M at $2.96B post — the largest mineral-exploration venture round on record, anchoring KoBold as the AI-native critical-minerals comp to traditional majors Freeport-McMoRan (FCX), Rio Tinto (RIO), and BHP (BHP). Durable + T. Rowe leading signals crossover capital is treating Mingomba copper discovery as a pre-IPO setup, not a venture science bet. The thesis turns on whether ML-driven exploration produces a step-change in copper hit-rates versus a generation of seismic-only majors — a binary geological catalyst, not a software one.

company_description: Chinese humanoid robot developer behind the GR-2 platform. Also operates a rehabilitation robotics business line for clinical use.
co_investors: Zhangjiang Hi-Tech, Zhangke Yaokun Fund, Prosperity7 Ventures, Junshan Capital
robotnik_take: Series E at $1.1B post puts Fourier into the Chinese humanoid unicorn cohort alongside Unitree, Galbot, and Agibot — but valuation lags Spirit AI's $1.4B post-Series-A by an order of magnitude in funding efficiency. GR-2 platform competes with Tesla (TSLA) Optimus and Apptronik Apollo on the bipedal stack while rehab-robotics revenue gives Fourier near-term cashflow most peers lack. Guoxin/Pudong lead reads as state-municipal alignment; the bet is rehab-revenue funds the humanoid roadmap.

company_description: Builds medium-duty electric truck chassis from a clean-sheet design for delivery, work-truck, and motorhome applications. Order book of approximately 4,690 vehicles worth around $500M; founded by alumni of Canoo and QuantumScape.
co_investors: Tiger Global Management, ArcTern Ventures, THOR Industries, Coca-Cola System Sustainability Fund, Ridgeline, Maniv Mobility, Ironspring, Schematic
robotnik_take: $100M Series B against a 4,690-unit / ~$500M order book — backlog-to-funding ratio is the cleanest in the EV-chassis class, contrasting with Canoo's collapse and Rivian (RIVN) / Workhorse (WKHS) burn rates. Tiger Global + Capricorn co-leading alongside THOR (THO) and Coca-Cola system signals strategic-anchor customer validation, not pure venture optionality. Medium-duty is the segment Ford (F) and Stellantis (STLA) under-serve; Harbinger's binary catalyst is converting the order book into delivered units without the chassis-startup death-by-NRE pattern.

company_description: Develops humanoid and cognitive robots equipped with onboard AI software for industrial and service applications. Flagship product is the 4NE1 humanoid, a 5.9-foot bipedal robot designed to understand natural-language instructions and handle payloads up to 220 pounds.
co_investors: BlueCrest Capital, Volvo Cars Tech Fund, InterAlpen Partners, Vsquared Ventures, HV Capital, Delta Electronics, C4 Ventures, L-Bank
robotnik_take: At the time, Europe's largest humanoid round — NEURA is the European counterweight to Apptronik, Figure, and 1X, with Volvo Cars Tech Fund anchoring auto-industry pull-through. Lingotto (Agnelli family) lead reads as Stellantis (STLA) / Ferrari (RACE) strategic positioning, not pure financial. 4NE1 third-gen targets the same warehouse / light-manufacturing TAM as Apollo and Optimus (TSLA), but with German industrial customers as the LTM revenue base. The bet is whether European OEMs procure domestically before US-trained models cross over.

company_description: Develops Nova, a fully reusable two-stage medium-lift rocket. Both stages are designed to return and land for refurbishment. Targets US national security launch contracts (NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1) alongside commercial customers.
lead_investors: Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Glade Brook Capital
co_investors: Point72 Ventures, Woven Capital, 776, Industrious Ventures, Leitmotif, Y Combinator
robotnik_take: $260M Series C funds Nova rocket development and Cape Canaveral pad LC-14, the first US fully-reusable two-stage program after SpaceX. Comp set: Rocket Lab (RKLB) on partial reusability, Relativity and Blue Origin privately. The Breakthrough Energy + Glade Brook lead is a climate-aligned strategic syndicate signalling launch-decarbonization thesis. First Nova flight test is the binary milestone; subsequent Oct-25 Series D + Feb-26 extension validate investor conviction.

company_description: Operates a 'space infrastructure as a service' business — builds and operates satellites carrying hosted payloads for customers who buy capacity rather than buying their own spacecraft. Backlog exceeds $500M across commercial and government customers.
co_investors: Bpifrance, Foundation Capital, Temasek, Uncork Capital, Starburst VC, Supernova, Tribeca VP
robotnik_take: Unicorn round on $500M+ backlog — Loft is the hosted-payload comp to Planet (PL) and BlackSky (BKSY) on the recurring-bookings model, but differentiated by selling capacity rather than imagery. Tikehau + Temasek leading reads as sovereign infrastructure capital, not growth equity; Bpifrance participation flags French strategic alignment. The thesis: as launch cost collapses via SpaceX, satellite-as-a-service becomes the dominant procurement model for governments unwilling to operate their own birds. Execution risk is bus-supplier dependency, not demand.

company_description: Real-time multimodal transport visibility platform — software that tracks freight across road, rail, ocean, and air. Sells to shippers and carriers for supply-chain visibility; competes with project44 and FourKites.
co_investors: Battery Ventures, Partech, NGP Capital, Bpifrance Digital Venture, LFX, Shift4Good, Yamaha Motor Ventures
robotnik_take: $30M undisclosed tranche brings Shippeo total above $140M — competes directly with project44 and FourKites in real-time visibility, against the public-market read-through of Descartes (DSGX) and SPS Commerce (SPSC) on the supply-chain SaaS stack. Woven (Toyota) lead plus Yamaha Motor Ventures suggests Japanese OEM pull-through. APAC customer growth of 53% YoY is the only metric that differentiates Shippeo from project44; if APAC consolidation continues, Shippeo is the natural acquisition target for a logistics platform play.

company_description: Develops direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology using membrane-based separation for sustainable battery materials supply.
robotnik_take: $18M Series A on undisclosed lead — DLE category competes against Albemarle (ALB), SQM (SQM), and Standard Lithium (SLI) on the brine-extraction stack. Membrane-based separation is the differentiator versus solvent extraction; the thesis is unit economics at scale, not technology novelty. Sub-$25M tail round for the segment — the binary catalyst is a single commercial DLE plant demonstrating cost-down versus conventional brine evaporation.

company_description: University of Sheffield spinout building a universal robotics software platform — an SDK enabling cross-platform robot programming across different hardware vendors.
co_investors: Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II, Praetura Ventures
robotnik_take: $5M seed for a cross-platform robotics SDK — competing with ROS-derived stacks and Viam's horizontal platform on the developer-infrastructure layer. Northern Gritstone lead is UK regional-deeptech capital, not venture-velocity. Comp set thin at this stage but adjacent reads: NVIDIA (NVDA) Isaac, ABB (ABB) RobotStudio on incumbent toolchains. Binary: developer adoption before larger horizontal players capture the SDK layer.

company_description: Develops a pulsed magneto-inertial fusion approach using helium-3 and deuterium, with direct electricity generation from plasma rather than steam turbines. Holds a power purchase agreement with Microsoft for a 50 MW plant targeted for 2028.
robotnik_take: $425M Series F lifts Helion past $1B cumulative at $5.4B — pricing roughly parallel to Commonwealth Fusion ($6B at last raise) and well above TAE Technologies and Marvel Fusion on the inertial-confinement comp side. Microsoft (MSFT) 50MW PPA by 2028 is the only enforceable demand-side commitment in private fusion; that contract is also the binary catalyst — Helion either hits commercial first plasma against the PPA timeline or the valuation resets. Lightspeed + SoftBank lead reads as growth-capital signaling, not first-of-a-kind risk underwriting.

company_description: Builds the Blackbeard hypersonic strike weapon for the US Army and Navy. Founded by former SpaceX engineers applying high-rate, vertically integrated manufacturing methods to hypersonic missile production.
co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Lavrock Ventures, Cantos, First In, BlueYard Capital, Interlagos
robotnik_take: $70M equity + $30M debt Series A — ex-SpaceX team applying high-rate vertical integration to hypersonic strike weapons. Direct comp set: Lockheed Martin (LMT) and Raytheon (RTX) on the incumbent missile primes, Anduril and Stoke Space on the new-defense-prime model. Lightspeed leading with a16z, BlueYard, Cantos signals the Anduril-template playbook is being copied. The thesis: DoD pricing per hypersonic round will collapse if Castelion's SpaceX-style manufacturing transfers to munitions — a binary on cost-per-unit, not technology.

company_description: Japanese satellite system integrator scaling micro-satellite production for commercial and government constellations. Operates as a vertically integrated supplier of buses, payloads, and mission management.
robotnik_take: $52M Series B for Japan's leading micro-satellite integrator — comp set: Mitsubishi Electric (6503 JP) and IHI (7013 JP) on the incumbent Japanese aerospace side, plus Rocket Lab (RKLB) on the vertically integrated smallsat-bus model. Incubate Fund lead reads as Japan-domestic capital depth, not international growth signal. Thesis: Japan's MoD smallsat procurement is reshoring from US suppliers; ArkEdge is the most plausible domestic prime. Binary catalyst is the next JAXA / MoD constellation contract.

company_description: Builds neutral-atom quantum computers using arrays of optically trapped rubidium atoms as qubits. Spun out of Harvard and MIT research; customers include Japanese supercomputing centers.
lead_investors: Google, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Valor Equity Partners
co_investors: QVT Family Office, Safar Partners
robotnik_take: $230M convertible note led by Google (GOOG), SoftBank Vision Fund 2, and Valor — the cap-stack signal is that QuEra is being positioned as the neutral-atom leader against IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI), and D-Wave (QBTS) on the public-market side, plus PsiQuantum and Quantinuum privately. $41M Japan supercomputing-center sale is the only real commercial-revenue datapoint in modal neutral-atom. Convertible structure rather than equity reads as price-discovery deferral by Google — they want the option without setting the mark. Modality bet, not company bet.

company_description: Builds Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot for warehouse and manufacturing work. Partnered with Mercedes-Benz for factory pilot deployments; targets logistics and automotive industrial customers.
co_investors: Google/DeepMind
robotnik_take: $350M Series A at $1.5B post (later expanded to $403M) — Apptronik is now the Western pure-play humanoid comp to Figure, 1X, and Agility on the bipedal-warehouse stack, against Tesla (TSLA) Optimus on the integrated-OEM side. Google/DeepMind co-investing is the structural differentiator: Apollo gets a foundation-model partner most peers lack. Mercedes-Benz pilot is the early procurement signal. Binary catalyst is converting the Mercedes pilot into a multi-thousand-unit contract before US capital tightens on humanoid burn rates.

company_description: Designs analog in-memory compute AI inference chips, targeting energy-efficient inference for edge and client devices. Differentiated from digital accelerators by reducing the data-movement penalty that constrains GPU power efficiency.
co_investors: Samsung Ventures, In-Q-Tel, RTX Ventures, HH-CTBC (Foxconn/CTBC), Maverick Silicon
robotnik_take: $100M Series B for analog in-memory inference — comp set: NVIDIA (NVDA) on digital-incumbent, TSMC (TSM) as the fab partner, plus Mythic (private) and Syntiant on the analog-AI thesis. Tiger Global lead reads as growth-stage signaling, while Samsung Ventures + RTX Ventures + In-Q-Tel give defense and Korean memory pull-through. Energy-per-inference is the only credible angle versus GPU incumbents at the edge. Binary: a single tier-1 client SoC design-win demonstrating production-grade yield on TSMC nodes — analog-CMOS yield is the cliff that killed the prior generation.

company_description: Develops Mega-class high-power satellites — large, high-capability spacecraft designed for the heavy-lift launch era opened by Starship-class vehicles. Sells to constellation operators and government customers wanting more capability per spacecraft than current smallsat designs.
co_investors: Alpine Space Ventures, First Round Capital
robotnik_take: $110M Series B for Mega-class high-power buses — K2 is the post-Starship bet: bus capability designed around the launch-cost collapse SpaceX has now demonstrated. Comp set: Lockheed Martin (LMT) and Maxar (private) on the incumbent large-bus side; Rocket Lab (RKLB) and Loft Orbital on the new-entrant smallsat side. Lightspeed + Altimeter leading reads as growth-stage validation that the heavy-lift thesis is real. Binary catalyst is the first Mega-class delivery to a defense or constellation customer before competitors retool to match the payload class.

company_description: UK Cambridge University spinout designing gallium nitride (GaN) power transistors and ICs for industrial, data center, and automotive applications. Competes with Infineon, EPC, and Navitas in GaN power semiconductors.
co_investors: British Patient Capital, Parkwalk, BGF, Cambridge Innovation Capital, Foresight Group, IQ Capital
robotnik_take: $32M Series C against GaN power incumbents: Infineon (IFX DE), Navitas (NVTS), Wolfspeed (WOLF), and EPC (private) — Cambridge GaN is the smallest player in the public-market comp set by an order of magnitude. Strategic-investor lead with British Patient Capital signals UK domestic-semis support, not aggressive growth thesis. Data-center 48V conversion is the only segment where Cambridge GaN can credibly compete on volume; binary is a single hyperscaler design-win before Infineon's monolithic GaN ICs reach production scale.

company_description: Spanish developer of wavefront-phase imaging metrology tools for advanced-node semiconductor wafers, an alternative to traditional interferometry. Intel Capital is a strategic investor; launching the Phemet fab metrology tool from a new Tenerife cleanroom.
co_investors: Bullnet Capital, EIC Fund, Intel Capital, MONDRAGON Corporation, TEL Venture Capital
robotnik_take: $10.5M Series C for wavefront-phase metrology — competing against KLA (KLAC) and Applied Materials (AMAT) on the wafer-inspection stack, plus Onto Innovation (ONTO) and Camtek (CAMT) on the smaller-cap end. Samsung Ventures + Intel Capital + TEL Venture lead is the unusual signal: three of the largest fab and equipment customers are funding the same metrology supplier. Phemet tool's lateral resolution at advanced nodes is the binary. Sub-$25M round; deal economics priced for foothold, not category leadership.

company_description: Builds autonomous surface vessels (Spyglass, Cutlass, Corsair classes) for the US Navy and allied maritime forces. Founded by a former Navy SEAL; building Port Alpha, a dedicated autonomous shipyard for mass production of unmanned vessels.
co_investors: General Catalyst, Andreessen Horowitz, 8VC, Caffeinated Capital, NightDragon, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Point72 Ventures
robotnik_take: Port Alpha is the load-bearing piece — first new US Navy-grade greenfield shipyard in decades positions Saronic as the domestic shipbuilding picks-and-shovels play, not just an ASV vendor. Comp set: Huntington Ingalls (HII) and Austal (ASB AU) on hulls, Leidos (LDOS) and L3Harris (LHX) on integration, HavocAI and Anduril Marine private-side. $4B post is 4x prior round — pricing the unmanned-fleet thesis ahead of Replicator volume contracts and CHIPS-of-the-sea capacity build.

company_description: Operates an AI cloud service that rents NVIDIA GPU servers for AI training and inference. Manages over 25,000 GPUs across its data centers, adding Blackwell B200s in 2025; competes with CoreWeave and the hyperscaler clouds.
co_investors: NVentures (NVIDIA), ARK Invest, In-Q-Tel, Andrej Karpathy, Pegatron, Supermicro, Wistron, G Squared
robotnik_take: $480M Series D at multi-billion valuation funds Blackwell B200 buildout; 25,000+ GPU fleet positions Lambda as the merchant alternative to CoreWeave (CRWV) and hyperscaler AI clouds. Comp set: CoreWeave on listed GPU cloud, Crusoe and Together AI on private peers, Oracle (ORCL) on hyperscaler GPU rental. Capital intensity is the binary question — Lambda's lifetime raise sits a tier below CoreWeave's debt-heavy capital stack.

company_description: Finnish VTT spinout designing cryo-CMOS chips for control electronics in quantum computers. Targets the control-electronics layer that scales alongside qubit counts in superconducting and spin-qubit quantum systems.
co_investors: Voima Ventures, Lunar Ventures, Dhyan Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer VC, Atomico Angel
robotnik_take: EUR 15M equity + EUR 2.5M grants Series A — cryo-CMOS targets the qubit-control-electronics layer that has to scale with qubit counts. Comp set: Intel (INTC) Horse Ridge II on the in-house cryo-CMOS side, plus Quantum Machines and Zurich Instruments on the room-temp control side. EIC Accelerator lead is grant capital, not growth signaling. VTT pedigree gives Finnish national-lab fab access. Binary: integration with a major qubit vendor (IBM, Google, IonQ) before in-house cryo-CMOS solutions productize.

company_description: Develops high-performance RISC-V application processors for AI, cloud, and edge compute, founded by former Intel CPU architects. Targets per-core performance leadership in the RISC-V ecosystem.
co_investors: Maverick Capital, Fundomo, EPIQ Capital Group, Jim Keller (Tenstorrent CEO)
robotnik_take: $21.5M seed for RISC-V high-performance application processors — comp set: SiFive and Tenstorrent (Jim Keller) on the RISC-V architecture side, against Intel (INTC), AMD (AMD), and ARM (ARM) on the licensed/integrated incumbents. Eclipse Ventures lead plus Keller as angel signals architect-network capital, not platform-velocity yet. Ex-Intel CPU team is the thesis: per-core performance leadership in RISC-V has been the white-whale of the ecosystem. Binary catalyst is a tape-out demonstrating credible IPC against ARM v9.

company_description: Chinese manufacturer of photomasks used in IC lithography. Part of China's domestic chip supply push to reduce dependence on Photronics and Japanese photomask suppliers.
robotnik_take: $102M Series B for Chinese domestic photomask supply — direct comp set: Photronics (PLAB) and Toppan (7911 JP) on the global photomask incumbents, against domestic substitution targets like SMIC (981 HK) and Hua Hong (1347 HK) on demand-side. Investor list undisclosed but round size signals state-aligned capital depth. Photomasks are an under-appreciated chokepoint in China's semiconductor self-sufficiency push — the binary is whether Puzhao can serve advanced-node masks before US export controls tighten further.

company_description: Provides quantum control hardware and software — the OPX+ controller and QUA programming language — that orchestrate qubit operations. Customers include more than half of the active quantum computing companies worldwide, regardless of qubit modality.
co_investors: Intel Capital, Red Dot Capital Partners
robotnik_take: $170M Series C at $700M post — Quantum Machines is the Switzerland of quantum: serves more than half of active quantum companies regardless of modality. Comp set: IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI), and D-Wave (QBTS) on the public modality side; Keysight (KEYS) as the test-and-measurement analog. PSG Equity lead plus Intel Capital co-invest signals growth and strategic alignment. Thesis: control-electronics revenue scales with industry-wide qubit count, not modality winners. Picks-and-shovels at fair price.

company_description: Provides a horizontal software platform — a robotics and IoT operating system — for connecting and managing smart machines. Founded by MongoDB co-founder Eliot Horowitz; positions as developer infrastructure rather than vertical robotics.
co_investors: Battery Ventures, Neurone
robotnik_take: $30M Series C — Viam is the horizontal robotics OS comp to Physical Intelligence on the model layer and ROS-derived stacks on the open-source layer, plus PTC's (PTC) ThingWorx on the industrial-IoT-software side. Eliot Horowitz's MongoDB-derived playbook reads as developer-infra-first, vertical-application-second. Union Square + Battery + Neurone is a small-check insider round, not a growth-stage signal. Binary: whether Viam captures meaningful share of the OEM SDK layer before NVIDIA (NVDA) Isaac and AWS RoboMaker compress the developer-tooling pricing power.

company_description: Develops the Leonidas high-power microwave system for counter-drone and counter-electronics use. Sells solid-state directed-energy weapons to the US Army and allied militaries.
co_investors: General Dynamics Land Systems, StepStone Group, T. Rowe Price, NightDragon, Manhattan Venture Partners
robotnik_take: $250M Series D at $1.35B post-money positions Epirus as the best-capitalized pure-play HPM counter-drone vendor. Comp set: Anduril (private) on broader defense-tech, RTX (RTX) and Lockheed (LMT) on incumbent directed-energy, no public pure-play. Pentagon Leonidas IDIQ award is the binary catalyst. The 2x step-up from Series C signals continued defense-tech momentum through the autonomy procurement cycle.

company_description: Develops Hivemind, an AI autonomy stack for military aircraft and drones that enables operation in GPS- and communications-denied environments. Products include the V-BAT vertical-takeoff UAV and Hivemind-equipped fighter jet retrofits.
co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, US Innovative Technology Fund, Washington Harbour Partners
robotnik_take: $240M Series F at $5.3B post — Shield AI is the autonomy-software comp to Anduril on the vertically integrated defense-prime side, plus AeroVironment (AVAV), Kratos (KTOS), and Northrop (NOC) on the public-market autonomy stack. L3Harris (LHX) + Hanwha Aerospace co-leading is the structural signal: incumbent primes are buying influence in the software layer rather than building. V-BAT plus Hivemind-equipped F-16 retrofits make Shield AI the rare both-platform-and-software bet. Binary catalyst is the first Hivemind program-of-record award at scale.

company_description: Mind Robotics is a Rivian spinout building AI-enabled robotic systems for complex manufacturing tasks requiring dexterity, adaptability, and real-time decision-making, leveraging Rivian operations data as a foundation. Led by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe.
robotnik_take: $115M is an outlier seed — Eclipse Ventures anchoring an RJ Scaringe-led Rivian spinout with proprietary auto-manufacturing data. Comp set: Symbotic (SYM) on warehouse automation, Rockwell (ROK) on industrial automation, plus private peers Apptronik and Figure AI on the humanoid side. The Rivian-data-flywheel pitch is unique in the seed cohort — closest analog is Tesla's Optimus internal program. Four months later the Series A priced at $2B valuation with Accel and a16z, validating the seed thesis but pricing in the entire data-advantage moat upfront.

company_description: Builds Dexter, a smaller, mobile surgical robot for ambulatory surgery centers, designed to compete with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci on cost and footprint. FDA-cleared for gallbladder removal, hysterectomy, and hernia repair.
robotnik_take: $150M Series G — Distalmotion is the mobile-cost-disruption bet against Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) da Vinci, with Asensus Surgical (ASXC) and CMR Surgical on adjacent challenger cohort. Dexter targets ambulatory surgery centers — a segment ISRG's footprint and price point don't fit. Revival Healthcare Capital lead reads as concentrated late-stage healthcare-tech capital. Three FDA clearances (gallbladder, hysterectomy, hernia) is the commercial unlock. Binary: ASC adoption scaling procedure volume before ISRG counters with a smaller-footprint platform.

company_description: Develops the Photonic Fabric optical interconnect — silicon photonic chiplets that disaggregate memory from compute for AI clusters at higher bandwidth than electrical NVLink or Tomahawk-class switching. Targets hyperscalers building exascale AI systems.
co_investors: BlackRock, Tiger Global Management, Maverick Silicon, Lip-Bu Tan, AMD Ventures, Koch Disruptive, Temasek, Xora, Porsche SE, The Engine Ventures
robotnik_take: $250M Series C funds Photonic Fabric optical interconnect for AI memory-disaggregation; positions Celestial alongside Lightmatter and Ayar Labs as the merchant alternatives to in-house hyperscaler photonics. Comp set: Lightmatter ($4.4B), Ayar Labs (Intel-aligned), Marvell (MRVL) and Broadcom (AVGO) on CPO. AMD strategic LP is the load-bearing signal — accelerator incumbent hedging into optical I/O before HBM/copper power walls bind.

company_description: Danish developer of Direct Atomic Layer Processing (DALP) equipment for semiconductor, quantum device, and optics manufacturing. Tools deployed at NASA and ESA; partners include STMicroelectronics and Sony.
robotnik_take: $15M Series A — DALP positioned as the additive-deposition counterpart to ASM International (ASM NA) and Lam Research (LRCX) on incumbent ALD. STMicro (STM) and Sony (6758 JP) partnerships are the differentiator — these are tool-validation revenue, not pilot-conversion. NASA / ESA deployments are flagship references but small revenue. Sub-$25M round priced for tool-platform proof, not category leadership. Binary catalyst is a production-grade chamber qualified at a tier-1 logic fab.

company_description: Builds an AI-driven scientific discovery platform combining foundation models with automated laboratory experimentation for materials, chemistry, and biology research. Targets pharma and industrial R&D customers wanting closed-loop AI + lab automation.
co_investors: March Capital, ARK Venture Fund, Altitude Life Science Ventures, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority
robotnik_take: $200M seed is among the largest ever — Lila is Flagship Pioneering's biotech-platform playbook applied to AI + lab automation. Comp set: Recursion (RXRX) and Insitro (private) on the AI-for-drug-discovery side, Schrodinger (SDGR) on the in-silico stack, against Bruker (BRKR) and Thermo Fisher (TMO) on the lab-automation hardware. Flagship + General Catalyst lead reads as institutional conviction stacking, not seed-stage capital. The thesis: closed-loop AI plus lab robots produces faster materials/chem discovery than either alone. Series A bar is now extreme.

company_description: German laser-driven inertial confinement fusion company. Building a fusion research facility with Colorado State University to validate the laser-target approach in a research-to-commercial pathway.
robotnik_take: $55M extension — Marvel is the laser-driven-fusion comp to NIF on the inertial-confinement physics path, against Helion (magneto-inertial) and Commonwealth (tokamak) on the broader fusion-investment frame. EQT Ventures + Siemens Energy lead is the structural signal: Siemens Energy (ENR DE) gives Marvel a downstream grid-integration partner most fusion peers lack. Colorado State $150M facility is the research-to-commercial pathway. Binary catalyst is laser-target ignition demonstration on a non-NIF platform.

company_description: Builds Digit, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for warehouse and logistics work. Operates RoboFab in Salem, Oregon — a manufacturing facility targeting 10,000 robots per year — and deploys Digit in Amazon warehouses.
co_investors: SoftBank, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, DCVC, Playground Global, NVentures (NVIDIA), Sony Innovation Fund, Schaeffler, TDK Ventures, Safar Partners
robotnik_take: $400M Series C at $2.12B post — Digit is in active Amazon (AMZN) warehouse deployment, giving Agility the only confirmed multi-thousand-unit demand-side commitment in Western humanoid. Comp set: Figure, Apptronik, and 1X privately; Tesla (TSLA) Optimus on the OEM-integrated side. WP Global lead with SoftBank, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and NVentures (NVDA) co-investing reads as strategic-customer stack and supply-chain alignment. RoboFab 10K/yr target is the operational binary: hit the run-rate or the valuation resets versus humanoid peers still pre-production.

company_description: Develops the Versius surgical robotic system for soft-tissue laparoscopic surgery. The platform is modular — separate arms on independent carts instead of a single bulky tower — and competes with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci across more than 15,000 procedures globally.
co_investors: All existing major investors
robotnik_take: $200M tranche funds US FDA submission and commercial buildout for Versius soft-tissue platform. Comp set: ISRG (Intuitive) dominant incumbent, Medtronic Hugo and Stryker Mako on adjacent platforms, Asensus (ASXC) on listed peers. CMR is the best-capitalized private soft-tissue RAS challenger globally; US 510(k) clearance is the binary catalyst that unlocks the world's largest surgical robotics market and the path to a strategic exit or IPO.

company_description: Develops space-based solar power — orbital solar arrays beaming energy to ground-station rectennas using laser or microwave transmission. Targets defense and remote-power applications.
robotnik_take: $50M Series A for space-based solar — orbital arrays plus laser/microwave downlink. Comp set thin: no listed pure-play comp; adjacencies are Northrop (NOC) on space-power systems and First Solar (FSLR) on terrestrial PV. Index + Interlagos lead is venture-conviction capital. Defense and remote-power use cases are the only credible early markets — grid-scale economics remain speculative. Binary catalyst is a demonstration mission converting orbital power to ground-deliverable watts at any scale, on any timeline.

company_description: French composite recycling company recovering and remanufacturing carbon fiber from aerospace and automotive scrap into new structural materials.
robotnik_take: $56M Series B for carbon-fiber recycling — comp set: Hexcel (HXL) and Toray (3402 JP) on virgin carbon-fiber incumbents, Solvay (SOLB BR) on advanced materials. Aerospace and auto recycling is a structurally tight loop because virgin CF supply is constrained. Undisclosed lead limits read on capital stack quality. Thesis: recycled CF approaches feedstock parity with virgin as aerospace scrap volumes grow alongside narrow-body production rates at Boeing (BA) and Airbus (AIR FP).

company_description: Builds the Supernova satellite bus equipped with solar-thermal propulsion for rapid orbital maneuvering. Holds a $45M SpaceWERX contract; first Starburst-1 mission scheduled on SpaceX Transporter-18 in late 2026. Founded by a former SpaceX Raptor engineer.
co_investors: Mach33, FUSE, First In, TFX, Offline Ventures, Atypical
robotnik_take: $17.5M seed against a $45M SpaceWERX STRATFI commitment — backlog-to-equity ratio is unusually rich for a seed-stage space company. Comp set: Astranis and Loft Orbital on the agile-smallsat bus side, plus Rocket Lab (RKLB) on the vertically integrated benchmark. Solar-thermal propulsion is the technical differentiator — high specific impulse without electric-propulsion's power constraint. Ex-SpaceX Raptor CTO is the founding-team signal. Binary catalyst is the Starburst-1 mission delivery in late 2026.

company_description: Builds AI-powered industrial robots for heavy manufacturing applications. Sells robotic systems for high-physical-effort tasks; competes with FANUC, ABB, and Veo Robotics in the industrial-robotics segment.
robotnik_take: $5M seed extension with undisclosed lead — force-controlled assembly is the contact-rich category where FANUC (6954 JP), ABB (ABB), and Yaskawa (6506 JP) have entrenched position-controlled stacks but lack native compliance. Veo Robotics' collapse left the contact-rich niche open. Sub-$25M tail; undisclosed lead caps the signal. Binary catalyst is a single tier-1 manufacturer pilot before incumbents add native force control via firmware.

company_description: Builds full-sized autonomous unmanned ships for the US Navy. Targets the Pentagon's $2.1B Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) program; backed by GV.
lead_investors: Eclipse Ventures, Riot Ventures, Impatient Ventures
robotnik_take: $14M seed targeting the Pentagon's $2.1B MUSV program — direct comp set: Saronic (private) and Anduril on the autonomous-surface-vessel side, plus Huntington Ingalls (HII) and General Dynamics (GD) on the incumbent shipbuilders. Eclipse + Riot lead is defense-deeptech conviction capital. Amazon Robotics / iRobot / Navy founding team is the credibility signal. Binary catalyst is the first MUSV contract award — Saronic has the lead, Blue Water has the team.

company_description: Builds wall-climbing inspection robots and operates an AI software platform for industrial asset integrity. Sells to energy, manufacturing, and the US Navy for fleet readiness and infrastructure inspection.
robotnik_take: $125M Series D — Gecko's wall-climbing inspection comp set runs against Boston Dynamics' Spot on the quadruped side and ANYbotics on industrial walkers, differentiated by US Navy fleet readiness as anchor revenue. Read-through to industrial integrators: Emerson (EMR) and Honeywell (HON) on the asset-integrity software stack. Founders Fund leading reads as defense-aligned growth capital, not pure industrial. Binary: converting Navy contracts into multi-yard recurring SaaS before incumbents bundle inspection into existing CMMS platforms.

company_description: Builds software-defined ground stations for satellite communications, replacing dish-by-dish fixed infrastructure with a phased-array, multi-mission antenna platform. Targets defense and commercial constellation operators.
co_investors: Founders Fund, Also Capital, StepStone Group, BoxGroup, Humba Ventures, Balerion Space, Banter Capital
robotnik_take: $30M Series A — software-defined ground stations replacing dish-by-dish legacy infrastructure. Comp set: Viasat (VSAT), KSAT (private), and AWS Ground Station on the incumbent side; constellation operators Iridium (IRDM) and Globalstar (delisting in progress, Amazon acquisition) on the demand side. Alpine Space + a16z lead plus Founders Fund signals defense-tech infrastructure stacking. Binary: whether DoD and commercial constellation operators converge on Northwood's phased-array standard over AWS Ground Station.

company_description: Builds very-low-Earth-orbit (VLEO) satellites delivering 10 cm-resolution optical and thermal imagery. Sells to defense, intelligence, and commercial customers needing higher resolution than current LEO platforms can provide.
robotnik_take: $97M Series B — Albedo's 10cm VLEO resolution is class-leading versus Planet (PL), BlackSky (BKSY), Maxar (private), and Satellogic (SATL) on the public Earth-observation comp set. Defense and intelligence customers are the natural anchor demand; commercial demand remains uncertain at the resolution premium. Undisclosed lead caps signal-strength read, but $97M round size implies institutional conviction. Binary catalyst is the first commercial-grade VLEO satellite in operational orbit — VLEO orbital drag is the engineering chokepoint that has prevented this segment to date.

company_description: Develops applied AI and quantum software products in biopharma (drug discovery), cybersecurity (post-quantum cryptography), and materials science. Spun out of Alphabet in 2022.
co_investors: BNP Paribas, Google, NVentures (NVIDIA), Ray Dalio, Horizon Kinetics
robotnik_take: $150M Series E at $950M post — SandboxAQ is the diversified-applied-AI bet across drug discovery, post-quantum cryptography, and materials science. Comp set: Recursion (RXRX) and Schrodinger (SDGR) on AI-for-drug-discovery; Palantir (PLTR) on the applied-AI-platform model; CrowdStrike (CRWD) on post-quantum-relevant cybersecurity. Google (GOOG) and NVentures (NVDA) co-investing signals Alphabet-network continuity post-spinout. Three-vertical strategy is the structural risk: each vertical has dominant private and public competitors.

company_description: Manufactures productized satellite buses (Aries 100 kg class, Nova 200 kg class, Comet) for commercial and government customers. Targets cycle-time and cost reductions through standardized, mass-produced platforms rather than custom satellite designs.
co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Washington Harbour Partners, StepStone Group
robotnik_take: $200M Series C oversubscribed 3x — Apex is productizing satellite buses against incumbents Lockheed Martin (LMT), Northrop (NOC), and Maxar (private), plus Rocket Lab (RKLB) on the vertically integrated end. Point72 + 8VC leading with a16z signals crossover plus defense-tech conviction. $46M Space Force contract is the early procurement validation. Aries / Nova / Comet product lines target cycle-time and cost reduction. Binary: production cadence at the 500kg Comet class before SDA constellation procurement closes.

company_description: Builds autonomous orbital vehicles (the Jackal AOV) and ground software for space domain awareness and rendezvous-proximity operations. Sells primarily to the US Space Force and Department of Defense for orbital security missions.
co_investors: Meritech Capital, Eclipse Ventures, Riot Ventures, Menlo Ventures, 645 Ventures, ACME Capital, Space VC, Narya
robotnik_take: $260M Series C at $1.4B post-money cements True Anomaly as the best-funded private space-domain-awareness pure-play. Comp set: Anduril (private) on broader defense-AI, Rocket Lab (RKLB) Space Systems on on-orbit hardware, Slingshot and LeoLabs on SDA software peers. Four Jackal missions in 18 months is the operational tempo signal. SDA Tranche 2 / Golden Dome contractor selection is the binary near-term catalyst.

company_description: Operates a US standalone rare earth element refining plant in Massachusetts producing neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium oxides. Targets 500 tons per year of REE separation as a response to Chinese export controls.
co_investors: Escape Velocity, Builders Vision, Yamaha Motor Ventures, M Power, Presidio (Sumitomo)
robotnik_take: $76M Series B for the first US standalone REE refining plant — Phoenix targets 500 tons/yr Nd-Pr, Dy, Tb in direct response to China's export controls on heavy rare earths. Comp set: MP Materials (MP), Lynas Rare Earths (LYC AU), and Energy Fuels (UUUU) on the listed-REE side; USA Rare Earth (USAR) on the magnet-supply integration. Envisioning Partners lead plus Sumitomo / Yamaha strategic capital reads as Japanese off-take alignment. Binary catalyst is plant commissioning at 500-tons run-rate before MP Materials and Lynas expand heavy-REE separation capacity.

company_description: Develops critical mineral extraction technology for rare earth and battery metal recovery. Backed by In-Q-Tel, the CIA's venture arm.
robotnik_take: $10M seed led by In-Q-Tel — the CIA capital signal is the most relevant datapoint at this stage. Comp set: MP Materials (MP) and Energy Fuels (UUUU) on the listed-REE side; Phoenix Tailings (private) on the US refining-tech adjacency. In-Q-Tel's involvement signals defense / IC supply-chain interest in domestic critical-mineral extraction. Sub-$25M tail; binary catalyst is technical demonstration at pilot scale before grant-funding cycles compress.

company_description: Builds the Vector reconnaissance UAS — a fixed-wing vertical-takeoff drone for tactical intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance. Sells to European militaries including the German Bundeswehr; active in Ukraine in combat use.
co_investors: HENSOLDT, Airbus Defence & Space, Bullhound Capital, HV Capital, Project A, Peter Thiel, DTCP, Omnes Capital, Airbus Ventures, Porsche SE, Notion
robotnik_take: $176M Series C at $1B post — Europe's first dual-use UAV unicorn. Comp set: AeroVironment (AVAV) and Kratos (KTOS) on listed US tactical-UAVs; Anduril and Shield AI as autonomy-stack peers; Hensoldt (HAG GR) and Airbus (AIR FP) Defence as European partner-customers. Balderton leads European growth-stage capital; Hensoldt + Airbus Defence co-investing signals direct procurement pull-through. Vector reconnaissance UAS in active Ukraine combat use is the operational validation. Binary: NATO program-of-record durability.

company_description: Builds purpose-built humanoid robots for shipbuilding and industrial manufacturing. Partnered with HD Hyundai (the Korean shipbuilder) for shipyard pilot deployments.
robotnik_take: $27M oversubscribed pre-seed — Persona is the verticalized-humanoid bet for shipbuilding and heavy industrial. HD Hyundai (Korean shipbuilder) partnership is the differentiator versus generalist humanoid peers Apptronik, Figure, 1X, and Tesla (TSLA) Optimus on the warehouse-stack. Pre-seed round size signals strategic-customer commitment, not venture-velocity. Shipbuilding is a uniquely difficult humanoid use case — confined spaces, heavy payloads, harsh environments. Binary: a single shipyard pilot delivering measurable productivity uplift inside 18 months.

company_description: UK in-space manufacturing company producing semiconductor wafer materials — GaN, SiC, and other advanced compound semiconductors — in microgravity for terrestrial chip applications. Launched ForgeStar-1 in June 2025.
co_investors: World Fund, NSSIF, British Business Bank, Cardiff Capital Region, SpaceVC, TypeOne
robotnik_take: $30M Series A for in-space semiconductor materials manufacturing — comp set: Wolfspeed (WOLF) and II-VI/Coherent (COHR) on terrestrial SiC; Infineon (IFX DE) on GaN incumbents. Microgravity manufacturing of compound-semi wafers is a 30-year-old NASA thesis finally testing economic viability with cheaper launch. NATO Innovation Fund lead is unusual: structural alignment with European semiconductor sovereignty. ForgeStar-1 launch in June 2025 is the first commercial-scale orbital test of the thesis. Binary catalyst is recovered wafer quality versus terrestrial benchmark.

company_description: Building a constellation of orbital mirrors designed to redirect sunlight to terrestrial solar farms during the early morning and evening hours when solar power is otherwise unavailable. Sequoia's first space investment since SpaceX.
co_investors: Sequoia Capital, Starship Ventures
robotnik_take: $20M Series A for an orbital-mirror constellation — first space investment from Sequoia since SpaceX. Comp set thin: no direct public-market analog. Adjacencies: First Solar (FSLR) on terrestrial solar demand; Aetherflux (private) on the orbital-power concept. Lux + Sequoia lead is venture-conviction capital. The thesis: redirected sunlight extends solar-farm productive hours at marginal cost. Binary catalyst is a single in-orbit demonstration redirecting measurable lumens to a terrestrial site — speculative segment at every stage.

company_description: Builds radioisotope power systems using strontium-90 as the heat source for satellites, lunar landers, and undersea infrastructure. Targets locations where solar power is unavailable or unreliable.
co_investors: Seraphim Space, Balerion Space, JAWS, Vanderbilt University, RiverPark Ventures, 7i Capital
robotnik_take: $50M Series B with $60M+ in DoD/NASA contracts — Zeno's Sr-90 radioisotope power systems target satellites, lunar landers, and undersea infrastructure where solar fails. Comp set thin on the public side: BWX Technologies (BWXT) on naval/space nuclear, plus Lockheed Martin (LMT) and Northrop (NOC) on adjacent spacepower systems. Hanaco lead plus Seraphim Space and JAWS reads as space-deeptech conviction capital. 2026 nuclear satellite demo is the binary catalyst — first commercial RPS since the plutonium-238 supply collapse decades ago.

company_description: Develops physics-informed AI for chip design under the Artificial Chip Intelligence (ACI) platform, claiming around 75% cost reduction and 50% faster development timelines on chip projects. Competes with Synopsys and Cadence AI design tools.
co_investors: FPV, Candou Ventures
robotnik_take: $33M seed for physics-informed AI in chip design — direct comp set: Synopsys (SNPS) and Cadence (CDNS) on the EDA incumbents; Siemens EDA (SIE GR) on the third major; AspenTech (now part of Emerson, EMR) on the physics-AI cross-read. ACI platform claims ~75% cost reduction and 50% faster timelines, which is the binary: any of those numbers proven in a tape-out displaces incumbent EDA pricing power. Lux + Mayfield seed lead reads as deeptech conviction. Cognichip is the first credible AI-native challenger to Synopsys/Cadence in 20 years.

company_description: Builds silicon space solar cells with self-healing radiation tolerance for satellite power. Targets 1 MW per year of production capacity; competes with traditional III-V space solar suppliers (Spectrolab, Azur Space).
co_investors: Crosscut Ventures, Zeon Ventures, Mitsubishi Electric Innovation Fund, Airbus Ventures, Industrious Ventures
robotnik_take: $17M Series A on a silicon space-solar play against the III-V incumbents — Spectrolab (Boeing, BA) and Azur Space (private) own the heritage space-photovoltaic stack at premium ASPs. Silicon's pitch is order-of-magnitude cost reduction with self-healing radiation tolerance as the technical wedge. Airbus Ventures + Mitsubishi Electric (6503 JP) co-investing reads as supply-chain qualification, not pure venture optionality. Binary: 1MW/yr production translating to constellation design-wins at silicon ASPs.

company_description: Builds neutral-atom quantum computing systems and atomic-clock sensing products. Deployed at DoD and NASA sites; pursues both quantum compute and quantum-sensing applications for national security and intelligent systems.
co_investors: S32, SAIC, In-Q-Tel, Axial, Maverick Capital, NSSIF, Breakthrough Victoria
robotnik_take: $100M Series C at $1.8B post — Infleqtion is the dual-modality neutral-atom + quantum-sensing play against IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI), and D-Wave (QBTS) on the public side, plus QuEra and Atom Computing privately. $30M revenue with DoD/NASA deployments is the most material commercial-revenue datapoint in the neutral-atom cohort. Glynn + Morgan Stanley Counterpoint leading with In-Q-Tel signals national-security capital alignment. Binary catalyst is whether quantum-sensing revenue funds the compute roadmap before public-market quantum names raise the price-discovery bar.

company_description: Builds autonomous defense systems and the Lattice software platform that links sensors, communications, and weapons across battlefield domains. Products include the Roadrunner counter-drone interceptor, Ghost surveillance UAV, and Dive autonomous undersea vehicle. Sells primarily to U.S. and allied militaries.
robotnik_take: Founders Fund's largest check ever, at $30.5B post, prices Anduril above AeroVironment (AVAV) and within striking range of L3Harris (LHX) — a software-defined defense prime rerating. Comp set: Palantir (PLTR) on the data layer, RTX (RTX) and Lockheed (LMT) as legacy integrators, Helsing private-side. Arsenal-1 bets autonomous-weapons production scales like consumer hardware. The pricing reads as conviction the next DoD budget cycle reshapes prime-vendor share.

company_description: Develops the N1 brain-computer interface implant and the R1 surgical robot that installs it. Has implanted five paralysis patients to date; holds FDA Breakthrough Device designation for speech restoration. Founded by Elon Musk.
co_investors: ARK Invest, DFJ Growth, Founders Fund, G42, Human Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, QIA, Sequoia Capital, Thrive Capital, Valor Equity Partners, Vy Capital
robotnik_take: $650M Series E at $9.0B post — Neuralink stands largely alone among public-market BCI comps: Synchron (private) on the stentrode side, plus indirect read-through to Medtronic (MDT) and Boston Scientific (BSX) on neuromodulation. Five paralysis patients implanted plus FDA Breakthrough Device for speech restoration are the only material clinical datapoints. ARK + Founders Fund + Sequoia + QIA co-investing reads as Musk-premium pricing on a binary regulatory path. Catalyst is moving from breakthrough designation to PMA — trial scale-out determines whether $9B holds.

company_description: Builds in-space transportation vehicles — the Mira orbital tug for last-mile satellite delivery and Helios kick stage for direct-to-GEO transfers. Founded by former SpaceX propulsion lead Tom Mueller; targets commercial and national security in-space mobility.
robotnik_take: $300M Series C at $4.1B valuation makes Impulse the highest-priced private OTV/space-tug pure-play. Comp set: Astranis on small GEO, Astroscale (TYO:186A) on listed orbital services, D-Orbit and PAVE on European peers, no real US public pure-play. Mueller's SpaceX propulsion lineage is the technical moat; Helios Mars-class kickstage is the binary differentiator vs incumbent in-space transportation.

company_description: Designs the Callisto Analytics Processing Unit (APU), a chip optimized for big-data analytics workloads with claimed 280x faster throughput than CPU-based pipelines. Targets data warehousing and SQL workloads where GPUs are not the natural fit.
co_investors: 83North, Koch Disruptive Technologies, Pitango First, Viola Ventures
robotnik_take: $44M Series B on the analytics-processing-unit thesis — Speedata's Callisto chip targets the SQL/data-warehouse workload niche where NVIDIA (NVDA) GPUs are over-spec'd and Intel (INTC) / AMD (AMD) CPUs are under-spec'd. Comp set thin: Groq and SambaNova are inference-adjacent rather than direct. Walden Catalyst + Koch Disruptive co-leading flags strategic-customer interest in industrial-data pipelines. Binary: a single Snowflake (SNOW) or Databricks design-win demonstrating measurable cost-down on production analytics workloads.

company_description: Manufactures TRISO (TRistructural ISOtropic) nuclear fuel for advanced reactors. Built from the asset base of Ultra Safe Nuclear Corp.; targets the supply chain for high-temperature gas-cooled reactors and microreactor developers.
co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Washington Harbour Partners, Welara, Fundomo, Crucible Capital
robotnik_take: $42M seed built on Ultra Safe Nuclear's asset base — Standard Nuclear is the TRISO-fuel supply-chain bet for advanced reactors, against BWX Technologies (BWXT) and Centrus Energy (LEU) on the public-market nuclear-fuel stack. a16z + Decisive Point + Washington Harbour leading reads as defense-and-deeptech alignment, not energy-utility capital. The customer set is HTGR and microreactor developers — Kairos, X-energy, USNC successor entities. Binary: qualifying TRISO production for at least one DOE/DOD reactor demo before the advanced-reactor cohort thins.

company_description: Recycles rare-earth permanent magnets from end-of-life EV motors, wind turbines, and hard drives using its Mag-Cycle process. Operates Hub100, a first commercial demonstration facility, as a circular alternative to primary rare earth mining.
co_investors: ArcTern Ventures, Energy Impact Partners
robotnik_take: $25M tranche with Amazon and Microsoft (MSFT) co-leading — customer-as-investor is the differentiator versus primary REE plays like MP Materials (MP) and Lynas (LYC AU). Cyclic's Mag-Cycle process targets the recycled-magnet supply chain for hyperscaler-driven motor demand: EV traction plus wind generators feeding data-center cooling and robotics actuators. ArcTern + Energy Impact Partners reads as climate-infrastructure capital. Binary: scaling Hub100 to commercial throughput while primary REE prices remain volatile from MP and Lynas output.

company_description: Develops a stellarator fusion reactor design, spun out of the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics. Targets the German energy-industrial market with a high-temperature-superconductor-magnet stellarator approach distinct from tokamaks.
co_investors: UVC Partners, DTCF, Plural, Leitmotif, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Bayern Kapital, HTGF, Omnes Capital, Elaia, Redalpine
robotnik_take: $150M Series A — Europe's largest private fusion round and the leading stellarator bet against Helion, Commonwealth Fusion, and TAE on the tokamak/FRC side. Max Planck IPP heritage gives Proxima the only stellarator stack with a public-sector physics base (Wendelstein 7-X). Cherry + Balderton co-leading with Lightspeed + Plural is the European deeptech consortium pattern, distinct from the Microsoft (MSFT) PPA model anchoring Helion. Binary: HTS-magnet stellarator engineering closing faster than tokamak rivals — geometry vs incumbent capital.

company_description: Builds radiation-hardened AI edge computing systems for satellites and space-based applications. Targets onboard inference and data processing for LEO constellation operators.
robotnik_take: $8.4M seed for rad-hard AI edge compute — comp set: BAE Systems (BA. LN) and Microchip (MCHP) on the incumbent rad-hard MCU/FPGA stack, plus NVIDIA (NVDA) Jetson on the AI-edge side which lacks space qualification. Kindred lead is thin signal on its own. Sub-$25M tail; LEO constellation operators are the only credible customer base near-term. Binary: a single constellation design-win before rad-hardened Jetson variants reach market.

company_description: Develops a general-purpose robot foundation model — a single AI 'brain' designed to work across different robot bodies. Pittsburgh-based; targets robot OEMs and integrators that want to license the underlying control intelligence rather than build it in-house.
co_investors: NVIDIA, Samsung, LG, Hanwha, Mirae Asset
robotnik_take: $135M Series B at $4.5B post — Skild is one of two pure-play robot foundation-model bets (Physical Intelligence the other) against vertically integrated humanoid plays from Figure, 1X, and Apptronik. SoftBank lead with NVIDIA (NVDA), Samsung (005930 KS), LG, and Hanwha reads as Korean-conglomerate-plus-hyperscaler validation that robot-agnostic licensing is real. The bet: OEMs license the brain rather than build it. Binary: major OEM design-win against Figure's vertically integrated stack — licensing depends on humanoid leaders outsourcing the model.

company_description: Develops inertial confinement fusion using high-power excimer lasers, building on the laser approach demonstrated at the National Ignition Facility. Phoenix demonstration prototype targeted for 2026.
robotnik_take: $100M Series A — Xcimer is the inertial-confinement-fusion bet via excimer lasers, building on the NIF ignition demonstration. Comp set: Marvel Fusion (private) and Focused Energy on the laser-ICF side, plus Commonwealth Fusion and Helion on the magnetic-confinement stack. Hedosophia lead reads as growth-stage venture rather than energy-utility capital. Thesis: laser ICF inherits NIF physics while bypassing tokamak engineering constraints. Binary: Phoenix prototype demonstrating gain economics before magnetic-confinement raises the commercial bar.

company_description: Develops simulation, validation, and software development tools for autonomous vehicle and software-defined vehicle programs. Customers include 18 of the top 20 global automakers, plus defense and trucking autonomy companies.
co_investors: Franklin Templeton, QIA, Abu Dhabi Investment Council, Premji Invest, Stripes, Greycroft, General Catalyst, Fidelity Management & Research, Lux Capital
robotnik_take: $600M Series F at $15.0B post — Applied is the autonomy-tools comp to Mobileye (MBLY) and NVIDIA (NVDA) DRIVE on vehicle-intelligence, with 18 of top 20 OEMs as customers giving the cleanest enterprise revenue base in autonomy software. BlackRock + Kleiner leading with Franklin Templeton, QIA, ADIC reads as IPO-prep crossover capital, not venture. EpiSci acquisition extends from auto into defense autonomy. Binary: converting OEM tooling revenue into a defensible platform before vertically integrated rivals (Waymo, Tesla TSLA) commoditize simulation.

company_description: Develops AI software and autonomous systems for European defense, including a strike-drone family and software that processes sensor data for situational awareness. Sells to NATO ministries of defense with primary customers in Germany, the UK, France, and Estonia.
co_investors: Lightspeed Venture Partners, Accel, Plural, General Catalyst, SAAB, BDT & MSD Partners
robotnik_take: $692M Series D at $13.8B post — Helsing is Europe's most valuable defense-AI company and the counterweight to Anduril (private) on autonomous battle-management, with read-through to Lockheed Martin (LMT) and BAE Systems (BA. LN) on incumbent primes. Prima Materia (Daniel Ek) leading with Lightspeed + Accel + SAAB reads as European sovereign-defense capital. Altra battlefield-management plus strike-drone family extends from software into hardware. Binary: NATO procurement velocity holding through European rearmament before US primes dominate AI-prime category.

company_description: European satellite operator providing broadband and broadcast services from GEO and LEO orbits, including the OneWeb LEO constellation acquired in 2023. Anchor commercial partner on IRIS², the EU's sovereign multi-orbit broadband program. The French government holds ~30% of the company.
co_investors: Bharti Space, CMA CGM, FSP
robotnik_take: $1.55B with the French State doubling to ~30% — Eutelsat (ETL FP) is now a sovereign satcom asset, repositioning OneWeb LEO and GEO assets as European Starlink alternative against SpaceX. Public comps: SES (SESG FP), Viasat (VSAT), Iridium (IRDM) on satcom incumbents. Bharti Space + CMA CGM + FSP alongside Paris signals India-France-shipping strategic alignment. IRIS² anchor role is the only multi-billion-euro public-procurement contract in European LEO. Binary: IRIS² execution against a hostile capital market that has repriced incumbents from VSAT to IRDM.

company_description: Develops the ORYOM ophthalmic surgical robotic platform for cataract and other eye procedures. Israeli; running FDA trials toward a US clinical launch.
co_investors: Adani Group, Reiya Ventures, Fred Moll
robotnik_take: $125M Series B at $500M post pricing the FDA pathway, not the platform. Ophthalmic robotics has no public pure-play — exits route through Alcon (ALC), J&J (JNJ), or Stryker (SYK), with Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) the only standalone surgical-robotics comp. Eclipse Ventures leading after Adani strategic signals US clinical readout is the binary; Optos (parent Nikon, 7731 JP) is the imaging benchmark. Clinical milestones reset M&A pricing across the segment.

company_description: German developer of laser wafer dicing equipment with liquid cooling, producing higher yields for power electronics, photonics, and advanced packaging applications. Backed by Zeiss Ventures.
co_investors: ZEISS Ventures, NRW.BANK
robotnik_take: $13.5M Series A — LIDROTEC's liquid-cooled laser dicing targets the yield gap in power electronics, photonics, and advanced packaging where DISCO (6146 JP) and Applied Materials (AMAT) dominate the conventional dicing-saw market. Comp adjacency: ASML (ASML) on the broader EUV-and-fab-equipment stack. Lam Capital lead alongside Zeiss Ventures reads as semiconductor-equipment strategic alignment, not pure venture. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: a single tier-1 advanced-packaging fab qualification before DISCO ports liquid cooling into its incumbent stack.

company_description: Operates a real-time LEO ground station network supporting S, X, and Ka bands for satellite operators. Currently 15 antennas; targets 100+ by 2028. AWS is a partner; competes with KSAT and Viasat Real-Time Earth.
co_investors: Omnes, Expansion, CNES/SpaceFounders, Heartcore
robotnik_take: $17M Series A — Skynopy is the European real-time-ground-station bet against KSAT (private) and Viasat (VSAT) Real-Time Earth on the GSaaS layer, plus AWS Ground Station and Azure Orbital on the hyperscaler side. AWS partnership rather than rivalry reads as supplementary-network positioning. Alven lead with CNES/SpaceFounders signals French space-strategy alignment. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: scaling from 15 to 100+ antennas by 2028 before hyperscaler GSaaS commoditizes the entire ground layer.

company_description: Develops a universal robotics foundation model trained on synthetic data generated by a custom physics engine. Co-founded by CMU and Mistral alumni; targets robot OEMs needing a generalist control model.
co_investors: Bpifrance, HSG, Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, HongShan
robotnik_take: $105M seed — largest European-linked robotics seed on record and a direct foundation-model comp to Skild AI and Physical Intelligence, against vertically integrated humanoid stacks like Figure and 1X. Synthetic-data-plus-physics-engine differentiator inherits the NVIDIA (NVDA) Isaac Sim playbook but trained for general embodiment. Eclipse + Khosla co-leading with Schmidt + Niel + HongShan signals US-EU-Chinese capital alignment. Binary: cross-platform generalization on a robot the founders didn't design before peers reach foundation-model maturity.

company_description: Builds CivDot, an autonomous layout robot that marks construction site survey points with 8mm accuracy. Targets civil construction and earthworks contractors.
co_investors: Bobcat Company, ff Venture Capital
robotnik_take: $7.5M Series A — Civ targets the construction-layout niche where Trimble (TRMB) and Hilti (private) sell traditional total-station survey kits. CivDot's 8mm accuracy autonomous-marking format compresses what is today a two-person manual operation. Bobcat Company co-investing with AlleyCorp reads as construction-OEM channel validation. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: contractor adoption rates before Trimble integrates autonomous marking into its existing survey-equipment portfolio.

company_description: Swedish developer of the Kreuger 100 drone interceptor — a software-driven counter-drone effector designed to cost roughly an order of magnitude less per intercept than conventional missiles.
co_investors: SNO Ventures
robotnik_take: $3M pre-seed — Nordic Air Defence is the Swedish entry in the counter-drone-effector category against Anduril Roadrunner-M and Raytheon (RTX) Coyote on the missile-class interceptor stack. Kreuger 100's software-substitution thesis targets 10x cost reduction per intercept versus conventional munitions. Sub-$25M tail by an order of magnitude. Binary: any Swedish or NATO procurement contract demonstrating the economics before Anduril expands into Europe.

company_description: Chinese humanoid robot developer spun out of Tsinghua University, building the Xing Xing humanoid platform. Alibaba is a strategic co-investor signaling hyperscaler interest in embodied AI.
co_investors: HouXue Capital, Meridian Capital, Xianghe Capital, Crystal Stream Capital, Tsinghua Holdings
robotnik_take: $69M Series A — Robot Era is the Tsinghua-spinout humanoid bet in the Chinese unicorn cohort alongside Unitree, Galbot, Agibot, and Galaxea on the bipedal stack, against Tesla (TSLA) Optimus and Figure on the Western side. 200+ robots delivered is a material commercial datapoint most peers can't claim. CDH + Haier Capital co-leading with Tsinghua Holdings reads as state-aligned strategic capital, not pure venture. Binary: scaling STAR1/L7 deliveries against Unitree's price-leadership while ERA-42 brain proves out as a credible model.

company_description: French developer of the JEF photonic AI accelerator, processing data with lasers instead of transistors. Claims GPU-comparable performance at significantly lower energy; compatible with existing AI software frameworks.
lead_investors: Earlybird Venture Capital, Protagonist, Visionaries Tomorrow
co_investors: Generative IQ, C4 Ventures, Bertrand Serlet (ex-Apple VP), Christophe Frey (Arm), Olivier Pomel (Datadog), Thomas Wolf (Hugging Face)

company_description: Singapore-based developer of no-code robotics programming software that compresses process automation setup from weeks to roughly 15 minutes. Deployed in welding, abrasive blasting, and polishing across aerospace, maritime, and automotive industries.

company_description: Operates in-space manufacturing satellites that produce pharmaceutical and materials products in microgravity and return them to Earth in reentry capsules. The same reentry capsules also serve as hypersonic test beds for the US Air Force and NASA.
co_investors: Founders Fund, Peter Thiel, Khosla Ventures, Caffeinated Capital, Lux Capital
robotnik_take: $187M Series C funds W-Series in-space pharma manufacturing platform plus hypersonic reentry testbed contract pipeline. Three completed missions is the operational-tempo signal; FDA-pathway crystallization data from W-1/W-2/W-3 is the binary commercial catalyst.

company_description: Dutch developer of silicon-nitride photonic quantum chips, working toward the first universal photonic quantum computer planned for 2026.
co_investors: PhotonVentures, Oost NL, FORWARD.one
robotnik_take: $17M Series A — QuiX is the Dutch silicon-nitride photonic-quantum bet against IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI), and D-Wave (QBTS) on the public-quantum tape, plus PsiQuantum (private) on the direct photonic-modality side. Sub-$25M tail relative to PsiQuantum's $750M-plus rounds. Binary: 2026 universal-photonic-quantum delivery before PsiQuantum's silicon-photonics scale advantage closes the modality.

company_description: German developer of L4 autonomous driving software using a cognitive/neuroscience-based active inference architecture. EU-certified for European deployment.
co_investors: German HNWIs

EU certification is the regulatory differentiator. Segenia + eCAPITAL leading with German HNWIs reads as Mittelstand-aligned domestic capital. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: a single European OEM design-win demonstrating that neuroscience-based architecture beats scale-driven approaches on regulated roads.

company_description: Israeli defense-tech company building a tactical drone operating system and combat drones. Battle-tested with the Israel Defense Forces in Gaza and under US Department of Defense contracts.
co_investors: Claltech (Blavatnik), Union-Tech Ventures, Chartered Group
robotnik_take: $30M Series B extension funds US DoD scale-up; XTEND's tactical-drone AI is in active operational use across IDF, US, Singapore. Sole-source deployment posture inside three militaries is the moat; Replicator program selection is the binary US procurement catalyst.

NTT + Qatar Investment Authority lead reads as Japan-Gulf sovereign capital. Binary: global expansion from Japan-anchor base monetizing the controller layer.

company_description: Builds the Bedrock Operator, a retrofit autonomy kit that converts 20-80 ton excavators into autonomous earth-moving machines. Founded by former Waymo engineers; sells to construction and earthworks contractors.

Binary: contractor adoption rates before CAT's Autonomy roadmap matures into a native offering.

company_description: Builds expeditionary 3D-printed drones intended for in-theater manufacture by US and allied forces, targeting build cycles of under nine hours from spool to flight. Sells to DoD as part of the attritable-systems wave.
co_investors: Lockheed Martin Ventures, Decisive Point, Washington Harbour Partners, Booz Allen Ventures
robotnik_take: $47M Series A on a $100M USAF IDIQ base — Firestorm is the in-theater-manufacturing drone bet against AeroVironment (AVAV), Kratos (KTOS), and Anduril (private) on the attritable stack. xCell containerized micro-factory targets sub-9-hour spool-to-flight cycles, addressing the supply-chain vulnerability the Ukraine war exposed. NEA lead with Lockheed Martin (LMT) Ventures, Decisive Point, Booz Allen reads as defense-industrial alignment. Binary: scaling xCell to fleet level before incumbents adopt distributed manufacturing themselves.

robotnik_take: $12M seed — Bone AI is the Korean NDAA-aligned defense-drone bet against domestic incumbent Hanwha Systems (012450 KS) and US comp AeroVironment (AVAV) on the tactical-UAS export tier, plus Shield AI and Anduril on the allied autonomy stack. Third Prime lead with Kolon strategic reads as Korean conglomerate channel-plus-export capital. Above-median for Korean defense-tech seed. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: Korean MND procurement and a first allied-export contract validating the playbook.

company_description: French developer of a cloud-native space operations software platform for satellite operators. Targets enterprise and institutional space programs; competes with Cognitive Space and legacy ground segment providers.
co_investors: 42CAP, Karista, Qwaltec
robotnik_take: $11M Series A — Leanspace is the cloud-native space-ops-software bet for satellite operators, against Cognitive Space and Slingshot Aerospace on direct cohort, plus legacy ground-segment incumbents like Kratos (KTOS) and L3Harris (LHX). ISAI + Capgemini Ventures lead with 42CAP reads as French-European space-software capital with systems-integrator distribution pull. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: a tier-1 European constellation operator standardizing on Leanspace or an ESA contract validating the cloud-native architecture.

company_description: French in-orbit servicing company offering life extension for geostationary satellites through rendezvous and docking. Competes with Northrop Grumman MEV and Astroscale in commercial satellite servicing.
co_investors: EIC Fund, IRDI, Newfund, Balnord
robotnik_take: EUR44M Series A extension — Infinite Orbits is the European in-orbit-servicing bet for GEO life extension, against Northrop Grumman (NOC) MEV and Astroscale (186A JP) on the commercial-servicing cohort, plus Maxar (private) on satellite-services adjacency. Matterwave + Wind Capital lead with EIC Fund reads as European-sovereign deeptech-plus-defense capital. Sub-$25M-adjacent. Binary: first commercial GEO life-extension mission executing on schedule before NOC and 186A JP capture incumbents-of-choice positioning.

company_description: Develops the industry's first power-delivery chiplet that integrates voltage regulation directly into processor packages. First chiplets manufactured at TSMC; claims around 50% reduction in total compute power.
co_investors: Pat Gelsinger (ex-Intel CEO)
robotnik_take: $25M Series A — PowerLattice is the power-delivery-chiplet bet, integrating voltage regulation into the processor package to cut total compute power ~50%, against incumbent voltage-regulator stacks from Monolithic Power (MPWR), Texas Instruments (TXN), and Infineon (IFX DE). First silicon at TSMC (TSM). Playground + Celesta lead with Pat Gelsinger as advisor reads as Intel-ex deep-silicon capital. Energy-per-token is the AI-fab economic constraint. Binary: a tier-1 AI-ASIC design partner before incumbents add chiplet-class regulation natively.

company_description: French semiconductor startup building optical interposer technology using nanolasers for chiplet-to-chiplet interconnect. Targets the AI/HPC packaging bottleneck addressed by Ayar Labs and Lightmatter.
co_investors: Maverick Silicon, PhotonVentures, Verve Ventures, Elaia, Earlybird Venture Capital, OVNI
robotnik_take: $18M seed positions NcodiN as the French chiplet-photonic-interconnect bet against Ayar Labs (private) and Lightmatter (private) merchant peers, with Celestial AI on the broader CPO race. MIG Capital + PhotonVentures + Earlybird syndicate signals European deeptech is funding silicon-photonics packaging before AMD/Intel (INTC)/Nvidia (NVDA) lock into proprietary chiplet stacks. The bet is whether merchant optical interposer IP wins before hyperscaler-captive vendors crowd out the seed cohort.

company_description: Builds liquid rocket engines as an independent supplier, including the Hadley (small launch class) and Ripley (medium-lift) engines. Customers include ABL Space Systems, Stratolaunch, and Phantom Space; growing hypersonic and defense propulsion lines.
co_investors: Woodline Partners, Principia Growth, XN, Alsop Louie Partners; +$50M debt
robotnik_take: $100M Series E at $600M post, plus $50M debt — Ursa Major is the independent-engine bet against Aerojet Rocketdyne (now part of L3Harris, LHX) and SpaceX (private) on US rocket-propulsion supply, with Rocket Lab (RKLB) vertically-integrated. Hadley/Ripley engines feed ABL, Stratolaunch, and Phantom; hypersonic-defense propulsion is the fastest-growing line. Eclipse lead with Woodline, Principia, and XN reads as deep-tech-plus-defense crossover capital. Binary: hypersonic backlog conversion before primes vertical-integrate engines.

company_description: Swiss humanoid robotics company developing dexterous manipulation platforms and the underlying control software. Competes with Figure AI, 1X Technologies, and Apptronik on humanoid platforms.
co_investors: NVentures (NVIDIA), Prosus Ventures, Redalpine, Moonfire
robotnik_take: $50M Series A — Flexion is the Swiss dexterous-humanoid bet against Figure AI, 1X Technologies, Apptronik, and Sanctuary AI on the Western humanoid cohort, with Tesla (TSLA) Optimus on incumbent reference. DST Global lead with NVentures (NVDA), Prosus, Redalpine, and Moonfire reads as growth-plus-NVIDIA-strategic capital backing a non-US humanoid platform. European-control-software heritage is the wedge. Binary: first commercial pilot deployments and a manufacturing partnership before Western cohort consolidates around 2-3 platforms.

company_description: Provides a precision positioning platform for autonomous vehicles and robotics, delivering centimeter-grade location through a global GNSS-corrections network. Competes with Trimble and u-blox in high-precision navigation.
co_investors: IA Ventures, UP Partners, Alumni Ventures
robotnik_take: $35M Series C at $230M post — Point One is the GNSS-corrections-network bet for centimeter-grade positioning, against Trimble (TRMB) and u-blox (UBXN SW) on the high-precision incumbents, plus Swift Navigation (private) on the direct cohort. Khosla Ventures lead with IA, UP Partners, and Alumni reads as autonomy-stack focused capital. Robotaxi and field-robotics fleets are the demand vector. Binary: integration into a tier-1 autonomous-driving stack or robotaxi platform before TRMB and UBXN SW bundle equivalent corrections natively.

company_description: French manufacturer of silicon carbide (SiC) crystal substrates for power semiconductors. Competes with Wolfspeed, Coherent, and Shin-Etsu in SiC wafer supply for EV power modules and industrial drives.
co_investors: EIC Fund
robotnik_take: EUR38M Series A — Zadient is the European SiC-substrate bet against Wolfspeed (WOLF), Coherent (COHR), and Shin-Etsu (4063 JP) on the global wafer-supply cohort, with II-VI (now part of COHR) and SK Siltron as additional reference. Credit Mutuel Impact + EIC Fund lead reads as French sovereign-deeptech capital — European EV power-module sourcing independence is the thesis. Binary: commercial substrate shipments and EV power-module qualification before WOLF's restructuring resolves and pricing normalizes.

company_description: Chinese humanoid robot developer targeting factory automation and service applications. Partnered with Unitree on embodied-intelligence development.
robotnik_take: $140M Series A — Robotera is the Chinese humanoid cohort bet alongside Unitree, Galbot, Agibot, and X Square Robot, with Tesla (TSLA) Optimus and Figure on Western reference. Unitree partnership on embodied-intelligence is the technical pull; Chinese-VC-led syndicate keeps it on the domestic-state-aligned axis. Factory-automation and service-application targeting matches the cohort norm of industrial-first deployment. Binary: scaled humanoid unit shipments versus Western cohort before the Chinese-Western humanoid markets fully bifurcate on export controls.

company_description: Builds the Vector reconnaissance UAS — a fixed-wing vertical-takeoff drone for tactical intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance. Sells to European militaries including the German Bundeswehr; active in Ukraine in combat use.
co_investors: Previous investors
robotnik_take: EUR208M Series C extension at $3.5B post — Quantum Systems is the European Vector-VTOL reconnaissance-UAS bet, against AeroVironment (AVAV), Kratos (KTOS), and Anduril on the Western tactical-UAS cohort, plus Turkish Baykar on the price-disruptor reference. Bundeswehr customer plus Ukraine combat-deployment validates the platform under fire. Balderton lead reads as European growth-plus-defense crossover capital. Binary: NATO procurement at programmatic scale before AVAV and KTOS introduce equivalent VTOL platforms.

company_description: Builds a decentralized satellite compute network combining trusted-execution hardware on satellites with cryptographic and confidential smart contract primitives. Targets orbital edge processing for crypto, AI, and confidential workloads.
co_investors: Superscrypt, Arbitrum Foundation, Nascent, Offchain Labs, Hashkey, Chorus One
robotnik_take: $10M seed — SpaceComputer is the orbital-edge-compute-meets-DePIN bet, combining trusted-execution hardware on satellites with cryptographic primitives, against terrestrial confidential-compute peers and traditional satellite-data-processing incumbents. Maven11 + Lattice co-lead with Arbitrum Foundation, Hashkey, and Chorus One reads as crypto-native crossover capital. Orbital-TEE is unproven hardware-plus-protocol. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: first on-orbit compute demo and token launch with enterprise-confidential-workload pull.

company_description: UAE developer of sovereign AI inference accelerators using open-source RISC-V cores. Targets GCC, Southeast Asian, and Global South markets seeking independence from US and Chinese chip supply; VLSI engineering team based in India.
co_investors: Undisclosed
robotnik_take: $10M seed — Mastiska is the UAE-led sovereign-AI-inference-accelerator bet on open-source RISC-V cores, against SiFive, Tenstorrent, and Esperanto on the RISC-V cohort, plus Habana (Intel, INTC) and Groq (private) on the inference-stack reference. GCC sovereign lead reads as petrostate-AI-infrastructure capital seeking US/China-independent silicon. VLSI engineering in India keeps cost structure competitive. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: first tapeout and a single GCC or Global South sovereign-cloud anchor customer.

company_description: Builds a robot learning platform that enables warehouse robots to acquire new tasks from human demonstrations. Sells to e-commerce fulfillment operators; competes with Covariant and Dexterity in warehouse manipulation.
co_investors: Fundomo, Neo
robotnik_take: $34M Series A — Tutor Intelligence is the warehouse-manipulation-from-demonstration bet against Covariant (acquired Amazon, AMZN), Dexterity, and Ambi Robotics on the warehouse-AI cohort, with Symbotic (SYM) and AutoStore (AUTO NO) on the broader logistics-automation reference. USV lead is unusual — the fund rarely backs hardware-adjacent companies, signaling conviction in the software-first manipulation thesis.
