Binary: deployment scale with a tier-1 e-commerce fulfillment operator before incumbents absorb demonstration-based learning into their stacks.

company_description: Builds AI-powered EDA tools for chip design automation and verification. Competes with Synopsys and Cadence on AI-enabled design workflows.
co_investors: Khosla Ventures, Eclipse Ventures
robotnik_take: $36M Series A — Vinci is the AI-EDA bet against Synopsys (SNPS) and Cadence (CDNS) on the EDA incumbents, plus Siemens (SIE GR) EDA and emerging AI-EDA startups like ChipAgents and Diakopto on the cohort. Xora Innovation lead with Khosla and Eclipse reads as deep-silicon-tools focused capital. The AI-EDA thesis is structural — verification cycle compression is the hyperscaler-design-team demand. Binary: a fabless tier-1 design-tool adoption before SNPS or CDNS folds equivalent AI workflows natively, or an acquisition by an incumbent.

company_description: Develops free-electron-laser (FEL) EUV light sources for semiconductor lithography. Spun out of SLAC and Stanford in 2022 to build an alternative to ASML's EUV light-source technology.
robotnik_take: $150M CHIPS Act grant — xLight is the US-domestic PIC-fabrication-capacity bet, slotting against GlobalFoundries (GFS) and AIM Photonics on the US PIC-fab tier, with Tower Semi (now Intel, INTC) on adjacent foundry reference. Commerce Department non-dilutive capital aligned with national-AI-infrastructure strategy. The gap in US PIC fab is real as AVGO/MRVL optical interconnect scales. Binary: facility milestones and first production runs converting grant into durable capacity ahead of geopolitical PIC-supply risk.

company_description: Belgian developer of compact robotic actuators and gearboxes for collaborative and humanoid robots. Competes with Harmonic Drive and Maxon in precision actuator components.
co_investors: Wallonie Entreprendre, finance&invest.brussels
robotnik_take: EUR3.8M seed — AILOS is the Belgian compact-actuator bet for collaborative and humanoid robots, against Harmonic Drive (6324 JP) and Maxon (private) on precision-actuator incumbents, plus emerging Chinese actuator suppliers on the price-disruptor reference. QBIC + HTGF co-lead with regional Belgian-French capital reads as European deeptech-hardware seed pattern. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: an integration partnership with a Western humanoid OEM before Chinese actuator supply scales into Western humanoid programs.

company_description: Designs RISC-V AI accelerator chips for edge and defense applications, with a focus on fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) acceleration. Competes with SiFive, Esperanto, and Tenstorrent in RISC-V AI silicon.
co_investors: Fusion Fund, Morgan Creek Capital, ADVentures (Analog Devices), Korea Development Bank, Rev1 Ventures
robotnik_take: $23M seed — Niobium is the RISC-V-AI-accelerator bet with a fully-homomorphic-encryption hardware angle for edge and defense, against SiFive, Esperanto, and Tenstorrent on the RISC-V cohort, plus Intel (INTC) on the FHE-research adjacency. Blockchange lead with ADVentures (Analog Devices, ADI), Korea Development Bank, and Morgan Creek reads as crypto-plus-strategic capital. Dayton, OH siting flags defense-adjacency. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: first tapeout and a DoD design-win before FHE-acceleration consolidates around general-purpose silicon.

company_description: Develops affordable welding and fabrication robots for small and medium manufacturers. Targets the SME industrial automation gap not served by Universal Robots or FANUC.
robotnik_take: $12M seed — Unlimited Industries is the SME-affordable-welding-robot bet, targeting a customer tier neither Universal Robots (Teradyne, TER) nor FANUC (6954 JP) serves cleanly, with ABB (ABBN SW) and Yaskawa (6506 JP) on the broader industrial-robot reference. a16z + CIV co-lead is unusually top-tier for an SME-industrial seed — signals conviction in the small-manufacturer underserved-segment thesis. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: unit-shipment ramp and a channel-partner agreement before incumbents introduce price-disruptor SKUs.

company_description: Develops an autonomous trucking platform for highway freight. Competes with Aurora, TuSimple, and Waymo in autonomous trucking.
co_investors: LAUNCH, Feld Ventures
robotnik_take: $7.4M seed — Autolane is the autonomous-highway-trucking bet against Aurora (AUR), Kodiak Robotics (now Ares Acquisition II, AACT), and Waymo on the live US cohort. Draper + Hyperplane co-lead with LAUNCH and Feld reads as classic seed-stage transportation capital. Entering a segment with several survivor incumbents and one prominent failure (TuSimple) — capital intensity and safety-case timelines are well-understood. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: a Texas-corridor pilot route and a shipper anchor before AUR locks lane-specific exclusivity.

company_description: Defense drone startup building autonomous off-road systems for military applications. Targets DoD SBIR/STTR contracts and operational deployments.
co_investors: Next Level Ventures, Midwest Growth Partners
robotnik_take: $7M seed — MACH is the autonomous-defense-ground-vehicle bet against Anduril, Shield AI, and Forterra on the autonomy-stack cohort, plus AeroVironment (AVAV) and Kratos (KTOS) on the broader unmanned-systems reference. TVC lead with Midwest growth capital reads as regional defense-tech seed positioning. Off-road autonomy is a structurally different problem from highway and air. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: DoD SBIR/STTR awards converting into a first operational deployment before larger autonomy-stack incumbents extend into off-road natively.

company_description: Builds physics-aware AI foundation models for understanding physical-world data — combining sensor, video, and time-series inputs into a unified physical-world model. Targets enterprise customers in manufacturing and energy.
co_investors: Bezos Expeditions, Venrock, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, Samsung Ventures, Systemiq Capital
robotnik_take: $35M Series A — Archetype is the physics-aware-foundation-model bet for sensor-video-time-series fusion, against NVIDIA (NVDA) Isaac, Google DeepMind, and Physical Intelligence on the physical-AI cohort, plus Skild AI on the robotics-foundation-model reference. IAG + Hitachi Ventures lead with Bezos Expeditions, Amazon (AMZN) Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Ventures reads as multi-strategic enterprise capital. Binary: industrial and energy enterprise deployments converting to recurring revenue before NVDA absorbs comparable physics-aware tooling.

company_description: Builds the Blackbeard hypersonic strike weapon for the US Army and Navy. Founded by former SpaceX engineers applying high-rate, vertically integrated manufacturing methods to hypersonic missile production.
robotnik_take: $350M Series B — Castelion is the hypersonic-strike weapon bet, founded by ex-SpaceX engineers applying vertically-integrated, high-rate manufacturing to Blackbeard production for the US Army and Navy. Comp set: Anduril, Lockheed Martin (LMT) hypersonic, and Raytheon (RTX) on the legacy primes. 20+ flight tests in 2025 is the production-engineering signal. Altimeter + Lightspeed lead reads as growth-defense crossover capital. Binary: Army/Navy programmatic procurement before primes win the consolidated hypersonic strike contract.

company_description: Operates the world's largest commercial synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation. Sells imagery and analytics to defense, intelligence, and insurance customers, with growing NATO-aligned demand for all-weather, day-and-night earth observation.
robotnik_take: EUR150M Series E (~$163M) — ICEYE operates the largest commercial SAR satellite constellation, against Capella Space (private) on direct SAR cohort, plus Spire Global (SPIR), BlackSky (BKSY), and Planet (PL) on the broader EO public tape. All-weather day-and-night imagery is the structural advantage as NATO-aligned demand scales on Ukraine and Indo-Pacific theaters. General Catalyst lead with Tesi (Finnish state) reads as growth-plus-sovereign capital. Binary: insurance and defense contract conversion before the commercial SAR pricing-floor compresses.

company_description: Italian company developing AI-powered prosthetics and humanoid robotic platforms, anchored by Italian sovereign capital (CDP Venture Capital). Competes with Ossur, Ottobock, and Open Bionics in prosthetics.
co_investors: AMD Ventures, Duferco, Eni Next, RoboIT, Tether
robotnik_take: EUR81M — Generative Bionics is the Italian AI-prosthetics-plus-humanoid bet against Ossur (OSSR DC), Ottobock (private), and Open Bionics on the prosthetics cohort, plus the broader humanoid reference. CDP Venture Capital lead with AMD Ventures and Tether reads as Italian-sovereign-plus-crypto-strategic capital — a landmark Italian robotics round. The prosthetics commercial channel funds humanoid R&D. Binary: European medical-device approvals scaling prosthetics revenue while the humanoid platform reaches first commercial pilots before Western cohort consolidates.

company_description: Chinese manufacturer of quadruped robots (Lynx, X20) and an emerging humanoid product line. Sells industrial inspection and service robots in domestic and international markets; competes with Boston Dynamics, Unitree, and ANYbotics.
co_investors: China Telecom, China Unicom, Yunhui Capital, China Fortune-Tech Capital, Zhejiang University Education Foundation
robotnik_take: $68M Series C — Deep Robotics is the Chinese quadruped-plus-humanoid bet against Boston Dynamics (private, Hyundai), Unitree, and ANYbotics on the global quadruped cohort, with Tesla (TSLA) Optimus and Figure on humanoid reference. CMB International + ChinaAMC lead with China Telecom and China Unicom reads as state-aligned financial-institution capital. Industrial-inspection plus emerging humanoid line is the dual-product wedge. Binary: international expansion holding versus export controls while the humanoid platform converts to commercial pilots.

company_description: Develops Mega-class high-power satellites — large, high-capability spacecraft designed for the heavy-lift launch era opened by Starship-class vehicles. Sells to constellation operators and government customers wanting more capability per spacecraft than current smallsat designs.
co_investors: T. Rowe Price, Hedosophia, Altimeter Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Alpine Space Ventures
robotnik_take: $250M Series C at $3.0B post — K2 is the Mega-class high-power-satellite bet for the Starship-class heavy-lift era, against Maxar (private, Advent), Airbus Defence & Space (AIR FP), and Ball Aerospace (now BAE Systems, BA. LN) on the legacy large-spacecraft incumbents. Redpoint lead with T. Rowe Price, Hedosophia, Altimeter, and Lightspeed reads as IPO-prep crossover capital. Capability-per-spacecraft is the thesis as launch costs collapse. Binary: first Mega launch and constellation-operator anchor contract before incumbents respond with new platforms.

company_description: German developer of quantum diamond sensing equipment for semiconductor metrology — using nitrogen-vacancy defects in diamond as quantum sensors for chip inspection. Competes with Bruker and KLA in advanced metrology.
lead_investors: German Federal + Bavarian Govts (European Chips Act)
robotnik_take: EUR178M government investment (European Chips Act) — QuantumDiamonds is the NV-defect-quantum-sensing-for-fab-metrology bet, slotting against KLA (KLAC), Applied Materials (AMAT) PDC metrology, and Bruker (BRKR) on the advanced-metrology incumbents. German federal + Bavarian sovereign capital is among the largest European quantum-sensing public investments. Quantum metrology adoption is unproven at production scale. Binary: integration into a tier-1 fab inspection workflow before incumbents add NV-diamond techniques to existing tool families.

company_description: Chinese precision motion control and actuator manufacturer producing components for robotics and automation. Targets Chinese humanoid robot OEMs; competes with Harmonic Drive and Nabtesco in precision actuators.
robotnik_take: $27.5M — ENCOS is the Chinese precision-motion-control bet, against Harmonic Drive (6324 JP) and Nabtesco (6268 JP) on the global precision-actuator incumbents, plus emerging Chinese actuator-supplier cohort. Huakong Fund + Shenzhen Capital Group lead reads as Chinese government-adjacent capital flowing into the robotics components layer. Domestic Chinese humanoid OEM supply is the channel. Binary: design-win contracts with Chinese humanoid OEMs at production scale before Japanese precision-actuator incumbents adjust price-volume strategy in the China market.

company_description: UK developer of a thermal-infrared video earth observation constellation for real-time monitoring of industrial emissions, energy use, and infrastructure heat signatures. Backed by NATO-aligned defense funds.
robotnik_take: NATO Innovation Fund leading is the cleanest pivot signal — SatVu's commercial industrial-emissions monitoring pitch is being explicitly repositioned as a defense-IR play, in line with the constellr defense-grade-thermal reframing the same month. Comp set: constellr on EU thermal-IR, Hydrosat on water-stress, BlackSky (BKSY) and Planet (PL) on listed EO. Constellation recapitalization after the 2023 HotSat-1 loss is finally clearing; the test is whether NATO-aligned contracts materialize before commercial revenue stabilizes.

company_description: Indian space situational awareness company providing orbital intelligence and debris tracking from ground and space-based sensors. Sells to government and commercial satellite operators; competes with LeoLabs and Slingshot Aerospace.
co_investors: Peak XV Partners, Kalaari Capital, Ronnie Screwvala
robotnik_take: $50M Series B — Digantara is the Indian space-situational-awareness bet against LeoLabs (private) and Slingshot Aerospace on commercial SSA, plus Spire Global (SPIR) and BlackSky (BKSY) on broader EO-data reference. 360 ONE + SBI Investment lead with Peak XV and Kalaari reads as Indian-Japanese growth-plus-Asia-strategic capital. Indian government and allied SSA programs are the demand vector. Binary: international government contracts and commercial satellite-operator adoption before LeoLabs and government-funded SSA programs lock in incumbent positions.

company_description: Designs analog in-memory compute AI inference chips that perform matrix multiplications directly in flash-memory cells rather than digital MAC units. Targets edge AI workloads in industrial, IoT, and automotive applications.
co_investors: NEA, Atreides Management, SoftBank, Honda, Lockheed Martin
robotnik_take: $125M Series D — Mythic is the analog-in-memory-compute AI inference bet for edge workloads, against NVIDIA (NVDA) Jetson, Qualcomm (QCOM) AI100, and Hailo on the edge-AI cohort, plus BrainChip (BRN AX) on the neuromorphic adjacency. DCVC lead with NEA, SoftBank, Honda, and Lockheed Martin (LMT) reads as long-cycle strategic capital absorbing the multiple resets. Production reset history is well-known. Binary: production ramp and automotive/IoT design-wins converting before edge-AI digital MAC roadmaps eliminate the analog efficiency edge.

company_description: Develops portable nuclear microreactors — semi-truck-sized 1 MW high-temperature gas reactors (Kaleidos) for remote installations and defense forward bases. Targets the diesel generator replacement market for the US Department of Defense.
co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, ARK Invest, DCVC, Founders Fund, Align Ventures, Chevron Tech Ventures
robotnik_take: $300M Series D — Radiant is the portable-microreactor bet (1MW HTGR Kaleidos) for DoD forward-base diesel-generator displacement, against BWX Technologies (BWXT), X-energy, and Oklo (OKLO) on the SMR/microreactor cohort. Draper + Boost VC lead with a16z, ARK, Founders Fund, and Chevron Tech Ventures reads as deep-tech-plus-energy crossover capital. Defense-distributed-energy urgency drives the round size. Binary: NRC licensing milestones plus a first DoD-deployed unit before incumbents move portable-class hardware through certification.

company_description: Operates a constellation of RF signal-intelligence satellites that geolocate radio emitters for maritime, defense, and intelligence customers. Detects dark vessels, jamming, and other RF activity invisible to optical or SAR sensors.
co_investors: SVB, Pinegrove Venture Partners, Hercules Capital
robotnik_take: $150M Series E — HawkEye 360 is the RF-SIGINT satellite-constellation bet for maritime, defense, and intelligence customers, against Spire Global (SPIR) and Kleos Space (private) on the RF cohort, plus BlackSky (BKSY) and Planet (PL) on broader EO reference. Dark-vessel and jamming detection is the structural complement to optical/SAR data. NightDragon + Center15 Capital lead with SVB and Hercules debt reads as cyber-defense-plus-venture-debt capital. Binary: NRO contract renewals and new constellation deployments before SPIR-class players extend RF SIGINT natively.

company_description: Chinese designer of general-purpose GPUs for AI and graphics applications. Public on Shanghai STAR Market; competes with NVIDIA and AMD in the GPU market, though primarily serves domestic Chinese customers due to US export controls.
robotnik_take: $1.1B IPO on Shanghai STAR Market — Moore Threads is the Chinese GPU-self-sufficiency listing against NVIDIA (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) on the global GPU tape, with Cambricon (688256 CH) and Biren (private) on domestic Chinese AI-silicon cohort. US export controls confine the addressable market to domestic Chinese customers. STAR Market float reads as state-aligned capital-market support for AI-self-sufficiency policy. Binary: next-gen GPU tape-out and Chinese-government procurement volumes validating the policy-anchored revenue base.

company_description: Swiss-US developer of chip-scale multiwavelength lasers that replace copper wiring with optical interconnects for AI data center scale-up. Pilot production planned for 2027; founded by Nobel Prize-contributing researchers.
co_investors: Y Combinator, Pegasus Tech Ventures, Protocol Labs, Halo Labs, Asymmetry Ventures, TRAC VC
robotnik_take: $15M seed — Enlightra is the chip-scale multiwavelength laser bet replacing copper with optical interconnects at AI-data-center scale-up, against Coherent (COHR), Lumentum (LITE), and II-VI (now COHR) on the laser incumbents, plus Ayar Labs and Lightmatter on the silicon-photonics cohort. Runa Capital lead with Y Combinator and Protocol Labs reads as deeptech-plus-Web3-crossover seed capital. Nobel-contributing research provenance is the technical signal. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: 2027 pilot production execution before NVDA/MRVL/AVGO lock optical-interconnect supply.

company_description: Chinese humanoid robot developer building general-purpose embodied AI platforms for industrial and service applications. Backed by China Mobile's Industry Chain Leader Fund; competes with Agibot, Unitree, and Tesla Optimus.
lead_investors: China Mobile Industry Chain Leader Fund
co_investors: CICC Capital, Chinese Academy of Sciences Fund, Suzhou Venture Capital, CMG Media Fund
robotnik_take: $300M Undisclosed at $3.0B post — Galbot is among the largest Chinese humanoid rounds, in cohort with Unitree, Agibot, X Square Robot, and Robot Era, with Tesla (TSLA) Optimus, XPeng (XPEV) Iron, and Figure on Western reference. China Mobile Industry Chain Leader Fund lead with CICC, Chinese Academy of Sciences Fund, and Suzhou VC reads as state-aligned-plus-academic-strategic capital. General-purpose embodied-AI is the platform pitch. Binary: mass-production timeline and enterprise pilot deployments versus Western cohort consolidation.

company_description: Chinese AI lab developing the Kimi large language model and consumer-facing chat assistant. One of China's leading LLM platforms alongside ByteDance Doubao, Baidu ERNIE, and Alibaba Qwen.
co_investors: Alibaba Group, Tencent Holdings, Wang Huiwen (Meituan co-founder)
robotnik_take: Notable for what's said — "rules out quick IPO" — more than the dollar amount. With Alibaba and Tencent both anchoring alongside IDG, Moonshot is now structurally a BABA-Tencent joint AI champion, not an independent. Comp set in Chinese LLMs: StepFun (state-backed), DeepSeek (privately funded), Zhipu, MiniMax, Baidu (BIDU) ERNIE. Kimi consumer pull is real; enterprise monetization vs API price compression is the open question. Less interesting as a fundraise, more as cap-table consolidation.

company_description: AI and chemical-informatics platform that designs advanced monomers and polymers for aerospace, defense, and high-performance industrial applications. Lockheed Martin Ventures is a strategic investor anchoring defense-supply-chain offtake.
co_investors: MVP Ventures, additional undisclosed investors
robotnik_take: Lockheed Martin Ventures co-leading with 8VC is the load-bearing fact — LMV anchoring an AI/chemical-informatics platform signals defense supply chain is now sourcing materials discovery the way it sources software. Comp set: Citrine Informatics on materials-informatics pure-play, Phaseshift on alloy discovery, Aionics on battery materials, plus Schrödinger (SDGR) on the computational side; Albemarle (ALB) is the only public proxy for advanced-monomer manufacturing. Aerospace and defense are the highest-margin verticals, and LM's anchor essentially pre-commits offtake.

company_description: Develops the LyteVision depth-sensing perception platform for autonomous mobile robots, robotic arms, robotaxis, and humanoids. Founded by alumni of the Apple Face ID team; sells perception modules and software to robot OEMs.
co_investors: Exor Ventures, Key1 Capital, VentureTech Alliance, Willenz
robotnik_take: Ex-Apple Face ID team building cross-platform depth-sensing for AMRs, arms, robotaxis, and humanoids is the cleanest hire-the-team bet in robotics perception this cycle. Comp set: Mobileye (MBLY) on AV perception, Outsight on solid-state LiDAR, Aeva (AEVA) on FMCW, Luminar (LAZR) on automotive-grade; Nodar on stereo vision. Fidelity + Atreides leading with Exor strategic (Agnelli industrial holding) is an unusual cap table — Exor's presence hints at Stellantis or CNH Industrial OEM design-win path.

company_description: Singapore-based battery materials recycling and upcycling startup focused on LFP cell recycling. Competes with Li-Cycle and Redwood Materials in battery recycling.
co_investors: CJIC, M7 Holdings
robotnik_take: Singapore LFP-recycling pre-Series A with SGInnovate and Shift4Good is sovereign-aligned ASEAN capital — LFP-specific positioning matters because LFP recovery economics are still unproven vs. NMC cathode value. Comp set: Li-Cycle (post-restructuring) on US Spoke-and-Hub LFP, Redwood Materials and Ascend Elements as the US incumbents, Cirba Solutions on US recycling, Princeton NuEnergy on direct cathode recycling; CATL (300750 CH) as the LFP cell-maker offtake counterparty. Pilot-plant commissioning is the binary milestone.

company_description: French defense-tech company developing autonomy software and mission systems for combat aircraft and drones. Anchored by strategic backing from Dassault Aviation; positioned as France's defense-AI counterpart to Anduril and Helsing.
co_investors: FirstMark Capital, Financiere Saint James, Kima Ventures
robotnik_take: Dassault Aviation leading puts a French aerospace prime directly on the cap table of a defense-AI software unicorn — closest analog is Helsing's Saab integration and Anduril's Lattice positioning. Comp set: Helsing ($12B private), Anduril, Quantum Systems on the European defense-AI side. Strategic frame is Rafale and FCAS autonomy: Dassault gets a captive software layer, Harmattan gets guaranteed program integration. €1.4B is rich for Series B but in line with European defense-AI peers post-2022 EU spend reset.

company_description: Develops a general-purpose robot foundation model — a single AI 'brain' designed to work across different robot bodies. Pittsburgh-based; targets robot OEMs and integrators that want to license the underlying control intelligence rather than build it in-house.
co_investors: NVentures (NVIDIA), Macquarie Capital, Bezos Expeditions, 1789 Capital, Disruptive, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Felicis Ventures, Coatue, Sequoia Capital, Samsung, LG, Schneider, CommonSpirit, Salesforce Ventures
robotnik_take: Largest pure robotics-software round ever and the clearest signal that capital is separating the robot-brain layer from the robot-body layer. Comp set on the brain side: Physical Intelligence (11B private), Rhoda AI (1.7B), Galaxea AI (2.9B in China). The strategic frame is OEM-agnostic licensing — a picks-and-shovels bet that the humanoid winners won't build their own foundation models. SoftBank-led syndicate alongside NVIDIA, Samsung, LG, Bezos is the most strategically loaded cap table in the cycle.

company_description: Designs the Sohu chip, a transformer-specific ASIC that hardwires the transformer architecture into silicon to outperform general-purpose GPUs on transformer inference. Manufactured at TSMC 4nm; targets inference workloads where transformer dominance makes specialization economical.
robotnik_take: Total raise approaching 1B for a pre-revenue ASIC bet on transformer architecture lock-in — the highest-conviction architectural wager in the dataset. Comp set: Groq (private, LPU on inference), Cerebras (wafer-scale), Tenstorrent on the alt-architecture side; NVIDIA (NVDA) as the architectural counter. If transformers stay dominant through 2027-28, Etched's Sohu economics are differentiated; if Mamba/SSM/diffusion architectures take meaningful share, the hardwiring becomes a liability. TSM (TSM) 4nm production timeline is the pacing constraint.

company_description: Builds a software-defined warehouse automation platform using climbing robots that move heavy material in three dimensions. Founded by former Tesla engineers; competes with Symbotic, AutoStore, and Exotec in ASRS.
robotnik_take: Avenir Growth leading solo on a $120M Series C at ~$570M is unusually concentrated for ASRS — growth-stage warehouse-automation rounds typically syndicate 2-3 leads given the capital intensity. Comp set: Symbotic (SYM) as the public benchmark, AutoStore (AUTO NO) on the public side, Exotec and Geek+ as private peers. Ex-Tesla founder DNA is the differentiator, and climbing 3D-movement architecture is genuinely novel vs grid-shuttle approaches. Fortune-100 deployment is the catalyst; SYM's operational stumbles open the comp window.

company_description: No-code frontline-operations platform for manufacturing and life sciences, with AI embedded in workflow apps for operators and quality teams. Sells to discrete manufacturers and pharma/biotech producers; Mitsubishi Electric is a strategic investor.
robotnik_take: Mitsubishi Electric leading at $1.3B unicorn signals Japanese industrial primes are buying their DX strategy rather than building it — the same pattern as Honda/Tulip and Toyota/Daido earlier in the cycle. Comp set: Siemens (SIE GR) MES, PTC (PTC) ThingWorx, Rockwell (ROK) FactoryTalk; AspenTech (now part of Emerson, EMR) on AI-enabled industrial software. No-code MES is consolidating around a small number of platforms, and Tulip's pharma/biotech traction gives it a vertical the legacy MES vendors are weaker in.

company_description: Chinese embodied-AI company developing dexterous-manipulation humanoid robots, including the PsiBot V1 wheeled dual-arm platform and the Psi-R series of vision-language-action models. Partnered with Meituan for the 'Little Yellow Bee' logistics robot and with NVIDIA on simulation training.
lead_investors: China Development Bank Capital, Guozhong Capital, CCTV Media Convergence Industry Investment Fund
co_investors: Xuhui Capital, Wuxi state-backed funds, Lanchi Venture Capital, Hillhouse
robotnik_take: Heavily state-backed syndicate (China Development Bank Capital + CCTV Media + Guozhong + Wuxi/Shanghai state funds) marks PsiBot as a designated national champion in dexterous manipulation — distinct from the strategic-corporate-led structure at Unitree or X Square (Xiaomi-anchored). Meituan partnership for last-mile logistics robot and NVIDIA (NVDA) sim-training collaboration are the commercial pull-throughs. Comp set: Galaxea (brain-layer), Unitree, Galbot on robotics; the dexterous-manipulation focus narrows the field meaningfully.

company_description: Chinese quantum computing company developing superconducting and NMR-based quantum systems for industrial and educational customers. Targets the domestic Chinese quantum hardware market under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
co_investors: Cornerstone Capital, Sichuan Zhenxing Group
robotnik_take: Guotai Junan Innovation Investment leading signals Chinese quantum is being treated as a state-priority sector under the 15th Five-Year Plan — the same financing pattern that mobilized capital into power-semis and EUV-adjacent equipment. Comp set: Origin Quantum, QuantumCTek (688027), QBoson on the domestic side; IBM (IBM), IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI) on the US public side. 40-country deployment suggests the educational/scientific tier is being commoditized faster than expected. Superconducting-revenue shift is the technical update.

company_description: Operates an autonomous drone delivery network for medical supplies, retail goods, and food. Started with blood and vaccine delivery in Rwanda and Ghana; now expanding US operations to Houston, Phoenix, and Seattle. Builds both the fixed-wing delivery drones and the operating software stack.
lead_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, Baillie Gifford, Valor Equity Partners, Tiger Global Management
co_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, Baillie Gifford, Tiger Global Management
robotnik_take: First close of a Series H at $7.6B post-money funds the US suburban rollout (Houston, Phoenix, Seattle) — the actual test of whether Zipline's economics work outside subsidized health-care delivery. Crossover-heavy syndicate (Fidelity, Baillie Gifford, Tiger, Valor) reads as IPO prep; closest public proxy is no one in autonomous delivery, with Wing (GOOGL subsidiary) and Matternet as private comps. Read this as the cleanest test of whether autonomous logistics scales without being acquired.

company_description: Builds metasurface-based optical AI inference chips spun out of Duke University. Uses metamaterial modulators much smaller than standard photonic foundry cells; competes with Lightmatter and Celestial AI in photonic compute.
co_investors: M12 (Microsoft), Carbon Direct Capital, Aramco Ventures, Bosch Ventures, Tectonic Ventures, Space Capital
robotnik_take: M12 (Microsoft) alongside Gates Frontier, Bosch Ventures, and Aramco Ventures is the load-bearing strategic signal — hyperscaler + diversified-strategic backing positions Neurophos as the most-validated alt-photonic architecture in the dataset. Comp set: Lightmatter ($4.4B), Celestial AI ($2.5B), Olix Computing ($1B), Q.ANT (Germany) on the photonic-inference side. The metasurface modulator approach is genuinely novel vs the Mach-Zehnder dominant architecture. Capital base ($118M total) is light for photonic-foundry economics.

company_description: Recycles rare-earth permanent magnets from end-of-life EV motors, wind turbines, and hard drives using its Mag-Cycle process. Operates Hub100, a first commercial demonstration facility, as a circular alternative to primary rare earth mining.
co_investors: Canada Growth Fund, additional existing investors
robotnik_take: T. Rowe Price leading a rare-earth-recycling Series C alongside Canada Growth Fund signals institutional capital is now treating REE recycling as a real industrial category, not an ESG-flavored thought experiment. Comp set: MP Materials (MP) on integrated mining + processing, Energy Fuels (UUUU), USA Rare Earth (USAR), Lynas (LYC AU) on primary processing; Noveon Magnetics and Phoenix Tailings on the recycling side. Chinese export-control overhang on REE magnets makes recycled feedstock structurally valuable to Western OEMs.

company_description: Chinese AI lab developing large language and multimodal foundation models. Backed by Shanghai SDIC, a state-aligned investor; competes with Moonshot AI, ByteDance, and Baidu in the Chinese LLM market.
co_investors: China Life Private Equity, Pudong Venture Capital, Xuhui Capital, Wuxi Liangxi Fund, Xiamen ITG Group, Huaqin Technology, Tencent, Qiming Venture Partners, 5Y Capital
robotnik_take: State-fund-led round at 718M makes StepFun the most explicitly Shanghai-backed of the Chinese foundation model champions — distinguishes it from Moonshot (Alibaba/Tencent anchored) and DeepSeek (private). Comp framing: Moonshot AI, Zhipu, MiniMax, and Baidu (BIDU) in domestic LLMs; embodied-AI extensions a likely next pivot given multimodal focus. Less interesting as a pure LLM bet than as evidence Shanghai is building its own state-aligned AI champion outside Beijing's orbit.

company_description: Builds an AI-driven semiconductor design platform that uses machine learning to generate chip layouts. Founded by the creators of Google DeepMind's AlphaChip, targeting EDA tooling and custom-silicon design services.
co_investors: NVentures (NVIDIA), DST Global, Felicis Ventures
robotnik_take: Series A at 4B for pre-commercial EDA — founder pedigree (DeepMind AlphaChip creators) is the entire thesis. Comp set: Synopsys (SNPS) and Cadence (CDNS) on the public-EDA side; Ricursive is positioned as the AI-native disruptor to both. The recursive self-improvement framing (AI designs silicon for next-gen AI) is fundable narrative but unproven; real test is design wins at hyperscalers building custom AI silicon. NVIDIA (via NVentures), DST, and Lightspeed lineup is conviction-stacked but reflects narrative more than commercial pull.

company_description: Builds software-defined ground stations for satellite communications, replacing dish-by-dish fixed infrastructure with a phased-array, multi-mission antenna platform. Targets defense and commercial constellation operators.
robotnik_take: Software-defined phased-array ground stations + $49.8M Space Force contract in parallel is the cleanest dual-validation in the satcom-ground segment — Northwood is being underwritten on DoD pull, not commercial constellation revenue. Comp set: KSAT, Viasat (VSAT), and Comtech (CMTL) on legacy ground stations; AWS Ground Station and Azure Orbital as hyperscaler counter; ATLAS and Leaf Space as private peers. Ground infrastructure is the unsexy bottleneck for the 10,000-satellite era, and DoD prefers single-vendor stack delivery.

company_description: German plug-and-play modular collaborative robot kits aimed at small and medium-sized manufacturers. Sells configurable robot cells with low integration overhead; expanding US presence with operations in San Francisco and Austin.
robotnik_take: German SME-cobot platform raising at growth scale despite legacy industrial robotics being mid-cycle weak — the bet is on plug-and-play modularity collapsing the SME integration cost that has been the binding constraint since Universal Robots scaled. Comp set: Universal Robots (Teradyne TER), FANUC (6954 JP), ABB (ABBN SW), Kawasaki on industrial robots; Vention and Mech-Mind on modular configurator software. Lightspeed + Lingotto (Agnelli) co-leading hints at Stellantis/CNH/Iveco distribution pull.

company_description: Develops AI-powered autonomous driving software for Class 8 freight trucks and robotaxis. Uses a simulation-first generative AI approach for training and validation, distinct from heavy-real-world-fleet competitors. Founded by Uber ATG's former chief scientist.
co_investors: Uber, NVentures (NVIDIA), Volvo Group Venture Capital, Porsche Automobil Holding, BlackRock, Radical Ventures, ADIA subsidiary, HarbourVest Partners, Incharge Capital
robotnik_take: Pivot from autonomous trucking alone to robotaxi expansion — competitive overlap with Waymo and Wayve widens. The simulation-first training approach differentiates Waabi from heavy-fleet competitors (Aurora AUR), but at 750M Series C Waabi is now committed to scale, not just R&D. Uber's $250M milestone-based check is the interesting structure: it's commitment-without-conviction and signals Uber is hedging across multiple AV partners (also a Waymo and Wayve investor).

company_description: Polish warehouse robotics company specializing in pick-and-place automation for e-commerce fulfillment. Competes with RightHand Robotics, Covariant, and Berkshire Grey.
robotnik_take: Series B extension with sole-lead Cogito Capital is conspicuously thin for a pick-and-place specialist three years after the original Series B — runway-extension framing reads as bridge financing rather than growth round. Comp set: Covariant on US AI-pick peers (acquired by Amazon in 2024), Sereact on EU peer, RightHand Robotics on US private, Symbotic (SYM) on listed-warehouse counter, AutoStore (AUTO NO) on goods-to-person. E-commerce automation TAM is real; Nomagic's positioning is squeezed between hyperscaler-backed Covariant successor and EU sovereign peers.

company_description: Blockchain platform decentralizing autonomous robotic labor markets via smart contracts and KNX tokens. Targets DePIN-style coordination of autonomous robots; positioned in the robotics-DePIN intersection alongside Auki Labs and GeodNet.
co_investors: Liquid Capital, Leland Ventures, Covey, LD Capital, M77 Ventures, Block Maven, Framework Ventures
robotnik_take: Robotics-DePIN intersection is a narrow but distinct category — Konnex sits between physical-AI infrastructure and tokenized labor markets, with Framework Ventures crossover signaling crypto-native conviction. Comp set: Auki Labs on spatial-AI DePIN, GeodNet on RTK-GNSS DePIN, Helium-IOT (Helium Foundation) on hotspot peer; Hivemapper on mapping DePIN. KNX token economics depend on robot-fleet onboarding, the binary risk. Modest by tokenized AI/DePIN standards — Bittensor and Render comparables clear at much higher capitalization.

company_description: Develops autonomous driving technology and operates commercial robotaxi services in multiple U.S. cities. Subsidiary of Alphabet; runs a Level 4 driverless ride-hail business under the Waymo One brand using a sensor-rich vehicle platform with custom lidar, radar, and cameras.
lead_investors: Dragoneer Investment Group, DST Global, Sequoia Capital
co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Mubadala Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Silver Lake, Tiger Global Management, T. Rowe Price, BDT & MSD Partners, CapitalG, Fidelity Management & Research, GV, Kleiner Perkins, Perry Creek Capital, Temasek
robotnik_take: Largest single AV raise ever; $126B post-money puts Waymo above most public auto OEMs and resets the bar for what a robotaxi unicorn is worth. Comp set: Tesla (TSLA) FSD as the only credible domestic rival; Baidu Apollo and Pony.ai (PONY) in China; Wayve and Waabi as private-market peers a tier below. Crossover-heavy syndicate (Sequoia, Dragoneer, Fidelity, T. Rowe) reads as IPO conditioning more than growth capital.

company_description: Designs wafer-scale AI processors and the systems that ship around them, including the CS-3 supercomputer and on-premises and cloud inference offerings. The wafer-scale approach packages an entire silicon wafer into a single chip with 900,000+ cores, targeting large-model training and inference workloads.
co_investors: Benchmark, Fidelity Management & Research, AMD, Coatue, Atreides Management, Alpha Wave Global, Altimeter Capital, 1789 Capital
robotnik_take: Pre-IPO mark at $23B sets the floor for the April S-1 at $22-25B — Tiger leading with AMD strategic alongside is the clearest signal Cerebras is preparing public listing inside two months. AMD's participation is the interesting tell: an architectural competitor putting capital in suggests AMD reads wafer-scale as complementary to its MI accelerator roadmap rather than substitutionary. Read this and the April filing as one event.

company_description: Designs the Atlas memory-centric AI inference chip, architected around high-bandwidth memory to run large language models at lower power than GPU-based inference. Competes with NVIDIA H100/B200 in AI inference workloads.
lead_investors: ARENA Private Wealth, Jump Trading, Unless
co_investors: Qatar Investment Authority, Arm Holdings, Helena, Valor Equity Partners, Atreides Management, DFJ Growth, Resilience Reserve, Flume Ventures, 1517
robotnik_take: Memory-bound architecture bet on AI inference economics — Positron's claim is <1/3 the power of NVIDIA H100 at comparable throughput. Comp set: Cerebras (wafer-scale), Groq (LPU), Tenstorrent, SambaNova on architectural alternatives; NVIDIA (NVDA) as the franchise to dislodge. Arm Holdings (ARM) on the cap table is the strategic tell — ARM positioning Positron as a chiplet partner for ARM-native inference servers. At 1B valuation, Positron is priced as a credible inference-share play but with substantially less validation than Cerebras or Groq.

company_description: Builds the Bedrock Operator, a retrofit autonomy kit that converts 20-80 ton excavators into autonomous earth-moving machines. Founded by former Waymo engineers; sells to construction and earthworks contractors.
co_investors: Xora, 8VC, Eclipse Ventures, Emergence Capital, Perry Creek Capital, NVentures (NVIDIA), Tishman Speyer, MIT, Georgian, Incharge Capital, C4 Ventures
robotnik_take: Retrofit-kit-on-existing-fleet model is the structurally smartest go-to-market in heavy-equipment autonomy — Bedrock avoids the OEM-displacement battle and rides Komatsu (6301 JP), Caterpillar (CAT), Hitachi (6305 JP) installed base. Comp set: Built Robotics (private, similar retrofit model), Caterpillar's own Cat MineStar, Hitachi (6305 JP), Komatsu autonomous truck programs. Ex-Waymo founding team carries an autonomy IP and recruiting moat. The 1.75B post-money is rich for a Series B but defensible if the retrofit kit ships in 2027 at promised cost basis.

company_description: Develops Nova, a fully reusable two-stage medium-lift rocket. Both stages are designed to return and land for refurbishment. Targets US national security launch contracts (NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1) alongside commercial customers.
robotnik_take: Extension on the Oct-25 Series D brings cumulative raise to 1.34B — Stoke is now the second-best-funded fully-reusable launch program globally after SpaceX. Comp set is narrow: Rocket Lab (RKLB) on the commercial side, Blue Origin private, Relativity privately. NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 award is the binary catalyst; without it, capital efficiency math breaks. First Nova flight test is the critical de-risk; existing capital base now buys ~3 years of runway through that milestone.

company_description: Develops the OTPU, a photonic AI inference chip targeting low-power, low-latency edge and data center deployments. UK-based; first products planned for 2027 shipment.
co_investors: Plural, Vertex Ventures, LocalGlobe, Entrepreneurs First
robotnik_take: UK photonic-inference unicorn at $1B — the round is more about staking out a European photonic-AI champion than near-term revenue. Comp set on inference-photonics: Lightmatter, Celestial AI, Q.ANT (Germany); Ayar Labs sits adjacent on interconnect. Strategic frame is sovereignty: Olix is the closest thing the UK has to a credible non-NVIDIA (NVDA) inference silicon bet, which is the only reason an undisclosed-lead $220M Series A clears. Valuation looks stretched without a foundry partner disclosure.

company_description: Builds Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot for warehouse and manufacturing work. Partnered with Mercedes-Benz for factory pilot deployments; targets logistics and automotive industrial customers.
co_investors: AT&T Ventures, John Deere, Qatar Investment Authority, PEAK6
robotnik_take: Mercedes-Benz on the cap table alongside Google and B Capital is the load-bearing fact — automotive OEM pull is the closest thing to commercial validation in humanoid right now. Comp set: Figure AI (2.6B+ private), Agility Robotics (BMW partnership), Tesla (TSLA) Optimus, 1X. At 5.5B post, Apptronik is in the second tier behind Figure but the Mercedes pilot makes it the highest-conviction Western humanoid bet for industrial deployment specifically. Series A extension at this size is unusual — implies Series B was a structural step Apptronik wanted to skip.

company_description: Operates a laser-based free-space optical communications network for satellite-to-satellite, satellite-to-ground, and terrestrial connectivity. Spun out of Google's Project Loon; sells to defense and constellation operators.
co_investors: DYNE
robotnik_take: Google (GOOG) Project Loon spinout valued at $1.3B with Battery + J2 Ventures + DYNE leading — laser optical comms is the AI-cluster-of-satellites equivalent for orbital networking, and Aalyria's Spacetime software is the routing brain. Comp set: Mynaric (now under Rocket Lab RKLB), CACI International (CACI), BridgeComm on optical terminals; SpaceX Starlink's internal ISL stack as the dominant proprietary architecture. Defense and constellation operators need a non-Starlink option; DPA Title III is the demand underpin.

company_description: Operates a proprietary weather satellite constellation and provides hyper-local weather prediction and analytics to enterprise customers. Targets aviation, logistics, energy, and government users with AI-native forecasts.
robotnik_take: Stonecourt and HarbourVest leading without a strategic anchor is the conspicuous feature — Tomorrow.io's pitch has long been enterprise + government weather analytics, but $175M Series F without an aviation or defense prime on the cap table means the constellation buildout is being financed on pure-PE conviction. Closest public comp Spire Global (SPIR) has struggled to monetize EO-derived analytics; the read-through is that weather-tech may be a single-name story rather than a category. DPA Title III tagging hints at DoD pull as the underwriting case for the constellation.

company_description: Builds commercial space station modules that will initially attach to the International Space Station and later separate as a free-flying successor station. Also develops a next-generation spacesuit for NASA's Artemis lunar program and operates private crewed missions to the ISS.
lead_investors: Type One Ventures, Qatar Investment Authority
co_investors: 1789 Capital, 4iG, LuminArx Capital, additional investors
robotnik_take: Hybrid equity + debt structure with QIA leading is the tell — Axiom is paying a debt-cost premium because pure equity at the prior implied valuation would mark down too aggressively against the Vast and Sierra raises in the same window. QIA participation is sovereign capital pricing optionality on Saudi/UAE crewed-mission revenue. CLD Phase 2 award is the binary; without it, Axiom is at risk of becoming a spacesuit contractor rather than a station operator.

company_description: Chinese humanoid robot company developing general-purpose embodied AI platforms for industrial and commercial applications. Competes with Galbot, Unitree, and Agibot in the Chinese humanoid market.
co_investors: Hone Capital, Cathay Capital, Meituan Dragonball, Capital Today, Beijing Automotive Group, InnoVen Capital, Loyal Valley Capital
robotnik_take: Galaxea is Beijing's answer to Skild AI/Physical Intelligence — same VLA foundation-model thesis, $1.4B places it in the same Chinese humanoid second tier as AI2 Robotics. Comp set: Skild ($14B Western lead), Physical Intelligence ($11B), Rhoda AI ($1.7B) on the brain-licensing side; Unitree, Galbot, AI2 Robotics on the hardware side. Jinding Capital lead alongside Meituan Dragonball, Beijing Automotive, and InnoVen is a strategic-heavy cap table. Chinese embodied-AI software is bifurcating from hardware OEMs the same way it has in the US.

company_description: Japanese lunar exploration company developing the HAKUTO-R lunar lander and Series 3 lander for cislunar cargo missions. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (9348). Not to be confused with the Chinese launch company iSpace / Beijing Interstellar Glory.
co_investors: Spring Partners, Chengdu Industry Group, Qianlima Capital
robotnik_take: Largest Chinese commercial launch raise on record; the entity name confusion (Chinese iSpace vs Japanese ispace 9348) matters less than the signal — Chinese state-aligned capital is funding reusable launch infrastructure as a sovereign capability. Closest public comps: Rocket Lab (RKLB) globally and Tokyo-listed 9348 in cislunar. The China launch race is a 5-name field (LandSpace, Galactic Energy, iSpace, Space Pioneer, Deep Blue Aerospace); this round consolidates iSpace as the top private. Export-control insulation is the structural moat.

company_description: German developer of weaponized drone systems for armed forces. Holds a Eur2.4B framework agreement with the German Bundeswehr, with deployment to a Lithuania-based brigade by end-2026. Founded in 2024 by Florian Seibel (formerly of Quantum Systems).
co_investors: 8VC, Doepfner Capital, In-Q-Tel, NATO Innovation Fund
robotnik_take: $1.2B unicorn mark on the back of a Eur2.4B Bundeswehr framework contract is government-pull at the cleanest extreme — Stark is being priced like a defense-prime in formation, not a venture-stage drone startup. Comp set: Helsing on AI-defense software, Anduril on US defense-tech, Quantum Systems (Florian Seibel's prior) on EU ISR drones, Tekever on Portuguese ISR, Shield AI on US autonomy; Rheinmetall (RHM GR) and Hensoldt (HAG GR) as the listed European defense-prime counterparts. Lithuania deployment is the binary execution gate.

company_description: Builds AI agents that automate semiconductor verification and design workflows. Strategic backing from TSMC-affiliated Matter Venture Partners; competes with Synopsys and Cadence on AI-enabled design tools.
co_investors: Bessemer Venture Partners, Micron, MediaTek, Ericsson
robotnik_take: Matter Venture Partners (TSMC-backed) leading with Micron, MediaTek, and Ericsson strategic is the strongest semiconductor-customer endorsement an AI-EDA startup has received this cycle — the buyer list is essentially the cap table. Comp set: Cognichip on AI-for-chip-design, Synopsys (SNPS) DSO.ai and Cadence (CDNS) Cerebrus on the EDA-incumbent counter, Quilter and Silimate on private peers. AI-agent automation of verification is the cleanest near-term productivity wedge for foundries at advanced nodes.

company_description: Builds large 3D world models — generative AI systems that produce navigable, physically consistent 3D environments from text or image prompts. Founded by Fei-Fei Li; targets applications in design tooling, simulation, and embodied AI.
lead_investors: Autodesk, AMD, NVentures (NVIDIA), Fidelity Management & Research, Emerson Collective, Sea
robotnik_take: Largest seed/early raise in spatial AI; Autodesk (200M anchor), AMD, and NVIDIA on the cap table signal this isn't a research bet — it's a tooling and simulation infrastructure play. Comp set is NVIDIA (NVDA) Omniverse and Google DeepMind's Genie work; the strategic frame is foundation-model layer for embodied AI training data, where simulation-generated 3D worlds become the bottleneck input. Fei-Fei Li brand premium is real but the 5B mark is rich pre-revenue.

company_description: Develops model-specific AI chips (the HC1) that hardwire the weights of a specific AI model directly into silicon, manufactured at TSMC. Claims much faster inference and lower power than general-purpose GPUs for a fixed model.
co_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, Pierre Lamond
robotnik_take: Cleanest expression of the model-specific ASIC thesis — Taalas hardwires a single model's weights directly into silicon, the most extreme architectural lock-in in the AI-chip dataset. Comp set: Etched.ai (transformer-specific ASIC), Groq and Cerebras (IPO filed) on broader alt-architecture, NVIDIA (NVDA) as the general-purpose counter. The structural bet is real: if a frontier model holds market share for 18+ months, hardwiring economics dominate GPU economics. Quiet Capital + Fidelity + Pierre Lamond is unusually deep-pocketed for an Other-stage round.

company_description: Chinese humanoid robot company developing AI-powered general-purpose humanoid platforms, including the AlphaBot embodied-AI product. Competes with Unitree and Galbot in the Chinese humanoid market.
co_investors: Yusys Technologies, Sentury Tire, Guotai Haitong Securities
robotnik_take: Baidu and CRRC co-leading is the load-bearing combination — Baidu brings the embodied-AI foundation-model stack (Apollo, ERNIE) and CRRC brings industrial-deployment scale at China's state-rail operator. Comp set in Chinese humanoid: Unitree (~$7B implied), Galaxea AI ($1.4B), Galbot, plus Tesla (TSLA) Optimus and Figure on the Western counter. Strategic frame is industrial-pilot pull: CRRC factory deployments give AI2 a customer the Western humanoid pure-plays lack. $1.4B places AI2 in the second tier behind Unitree.

company_description: Dutch fabless designer of edge AI inference chips for computer vision and LLM workloads in automotive ADAS, robotics, and industrial applications. Competes with Qualcomm, Hailo, and Intel Movidius at the edge.
co_investors: BlackRock, SiteGround Capital, Bitfury, CDP Venture Capital, EIC Fund, Samsung Catalyst Fund, Invest-NL
robotnik_take: European sovereignty play in edge AI — Innovation Industries + Invest-NL + EIC Fund signal Dutch and EU industrial-policy capital underwriting an alternative to Qualcomm (QCOM), Hailo, and Intel (INTC) Movidius. BlackRock leading the financial side is the unusual element; pension-fund capital entering EU chip sovereignty is the new structural pattern post EU Chips Act. Comp framing: Hailo (Israel, private), Mythic (US, private), Qualcomm and INTC on the public side. Automotive ADAS design wins are the binary; if Stellantis/VW/Mercedes commit, Axelera clears.

company_description: Designs custom AI ASICs optimized for transformer model training and inference. Targets large language model workloads at hyperscale, competing with NVIDIA GPUs and Google TPUs at the chip layer.
co_investors: Spark Capital, Triatomic Capital, Harpoon Ventures, Andrej Karpathy, Patrick & John Collison (Stripe), Alchip, Marvell
robotnik_take: Jane Street and Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness co-leading is the most ideologically loaded cap table in semis — high-frequency-trading capital + AGI-pilled fund underwriting a transformer ASIC bet. Comp framing: Etched.ai (similar architectural wager), Groq, Cerebras, NVIDIA (NVDA), Google (GOOGL) TPU. Alchip and Marvell as strategic investors signal a packaging/IP partnership path. Less polished story than Etched but stronger compute-customer pull narrative; the open question is tapeout execution at TSM.

company_description: Sells the SN40L AI accelerator chip and a full-stack enterprise AI platform combining hardware, models, and software. Targets enterprises deploying generative AI on-premises or in dedicated clouds, competing with NVIDIA DGX Cloud and Cerebras.
co_investors: Intel Capital, Assam Ventures, Battery Ventures, Gulf Development, Mayfield Fund, Saudi First Data, Seligman Ventures, T. Rowe Price
robotnik_take: Intel Capital's 100-150M check inside this round is the most strategically interesting element — Intel (INTC) backing a competitor's full-stack AI play either signals Foundry-customer positioning or platform-hedge against NVIDIA (NVDA). Vista leading at 350M reads as a private-equity-style structure on what was previously a venture round, implying SambaNova may be heading toward a sale rather than IPO. Comp set: Cerebras, Groq, NVIDIA DGX Cloud on full-stack enterprise AI. Less of a chip company than a platform play at this stage.

company_description: Chinese humanoid robot company developing bipedal humanoid platforms for industrial applications. Targets factory deployment pilots and government procurement; competes with Unitree, Galbot, and XPENG robotics.
co_investors: HongShan, Synstellation Capital, TCL Capital, 360 Capital, HouXue Capital
robotnik_take: Third Chinese humanoid round exceeding 250M in Q1 alone (alongside NEURA equivalent paths and Galaxea-class brain layer) — confirms China has entered the deployment-capital phase of the humanoid cycle while the US is still in foundation-building. Comp set: Unitree, Galbot, Xpeng (XPEV) robotics, Agibot. YF Capital (Yunfeng) anchor signals Jack Ma-network capital; Chaos Investment lead suggests state-aligned secondary. At 1.4B post-money on Series A, valuation is rich; depends entirely on government procurement pull-through.

company_description: Develops end-to-end embodied AI driving models that learn driving behavior from data rather than hand-coded rules. Licenses its self-driving stack to automakers and operates ride-hail pilots in the U.K., Germany, and the U.S.
lead_investors: Eclipse Ventures, Balderton Capital, SoftBank Vision Fund 2
co_investors: Microsoft, NVentures (NVIDIA), Uber, Mercedes-Benz, Nissan, Stellantis, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Baillie Gifford, British Business Bank
robotnik_take: The largest European AV raise and the cleanest test of the end-to-end learned-driving thesis vs Waymo's sensor-heavy approach. OEM-heavy syndicate (Mercedes, Nissan, Stellantis, Uber) prices Wayve as Tier-1 platform licensor rather than scaled operator — a fundamentally different unit-economics path than Waymo. Closest public proxy is Mobileye (MBLY); Wayve's $8.6B private mark looks reasonable against MBLY's market cap given the foundation-model architecture premium.

company_description: Luxembourg-based satellite IoT operator delivering 5G narrowband IoT connectivity through GEO satellites. Competes with AST SpaceMobile, Globalstar, and Iridium in satellite IoT.
robotnik_take: $29M EIB venture-debt at the InvestEU layer is non-dilutive growth capital, an unusual structure for a satellite-IoT operator — signals OQ is mature enough to support debt service, which Iridium (IRDM) and Globalstar (GSAT) only achieved post-listing. Comp set: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) on D2C scale, Iridium and Globalstar on listed satellite-IoT incumbency, Sateliot on EU peer. 3GPP 5G NTN standard adoption is the upside catalyst; the test is whether NB-IoT volumes ramp before debt obligations bite.

company_description: Builds an AI-driven test and evaluation platform for autonomous systems, used for validation of defense and autonomous-vehicle programs. Competes with traditional T&E vendors (National Instruments, Keysight) on simulation-first workflows.
co_investors: Redpoint Ventures, Thrive Capital, Felicis Ventures, Abstract Ventures
robotnik_take: $150M Series B at $1B for autonomous-systems T&E is heavy capitalization for an infrastructure-layer software business — Revel is being priced as the simulation-and-validation backbone for the defense-AV stack, not as a one-off vendor. Comp set: Applied Intuition (private, ~$15B) on AV simulation broadly, Foretellix on scenario-based testing, Ansys (ANSS) on engineering simulation; NI (now under Emerson EMR) and Keysight (KEYS) on legacy T&E. The DPA Title III tagging signals real DoD demand pull. Index leading without a defense prime on the cap table is the soft spot.

company_description: Builds modular cooling systems and TILES processors for space-based data centers. Targets orbital DC infrastructure alongside Lumen Orbit/Starcloud as a thesis on space compute.
lead_investors: Alpha Funds, KDDI Green Partners Fund, Unlock Venture Partners
robotnik_take: KDDI Green Partners Fund leading is the Japanese sovereignty-and-power-arbitrage tell — orbital data centers are a sovereign-power play for grid-constrained jurisdictions, and Japan is the most acute case. Comp set: Lonestar Data Holdings on lunar data centers, Lumen Orbit on US orbital DC, Axiom on station-attached compute, Starcloud on Starship-deployed scale; Equinix (EQIX) and Iron Mountain (IRM) as terrestrial counters. $10M seed sizing implies cooling-prototype demonstration is the near-term gate, not full orbital deployment.

company_description: Semiconductor spinout from Chinese EV maker NIO, developing automotive AI chips for self-driving and in-cabin compute. Competes with Qualcomm in automotive SoCs and with domestic Chinese chip designers like Horizon Robotics.
lead_investors: Hefei State-owned Investment, Hefei Haiheng, IDG Capital, China Fortune-Tech Capital, Hua Capital
co_investors: Hefei State-Owned Capital, Hefei Haiheng, China Fortune-Tech Capital, Yuanhe Puhua
robotnik_take: EV-OEM-to-silicon spinout pattern mirroring Tesla's Dojo and Xpeng's (XPEV) Turing chip — Hefei state-owned anchor signals Anhui province building its own automotive-AI cluster. Comp set: Horizon Robotics (9660 HK) as the dominant domestic ADAS SoC, Black Sesame, plus Qualcomm (QCOM) and NVIDIA (NVDA) on the foreign side. The strategic frame is China-domestic substitution: every Chinese OEM ultimately wants captive silicon, mirroring Apple's M-series strategy. Nio's first-mover advantage matters less than the volume committed.

company_description: Japan's flagship advanced semiconductor foundry, building a fab in Chitose, Hokkaido aiming for 2nm production by 2027. Technology transfer agreement with IBM; backed by Japanese government investment.
co_investors: Canon, Fujitsu, NTT, SoftBank, Sony, Development Bank of Japan
robotnik_take: Notable not for the dollar amount but for the 32-company private co-investor list — Canon, Fujitsu, NTT, SoftBank, Sony, and DBJ effectively coupling the Japanese industrial base to the foundry's survival. This is the closest the dataset gets to a national-champion equity structure; functions as commercial commitment as much as capital, mitigating the demand-side risk that has dogged Intel Foundry. Public read-through is bearish-at-the-margin for TSM and INTC if 2nm Rapidus volumes materialize on schedule.

company_description: Builds the Dream Chaser reusable spaceplane for cargo missions to the International Space Station, and develops satellites and orbital infrastructure including the LIFE inflatable habitat for commercial space stations. Increasingly focused on national-security space contracts.
robotnik_take: Pivot from commercial-LEO-station prime to national-security space contractor — Dream Chaser is now anchor to a broader defense play rather than the franchise itself. At 8B post-money, Sierra is valued in the same band as Axiom (350M debt+equity at similar level) and Vast (500M) but with a more diversified contract book. LuminArx leading without strategic primes participating is the soft spot — the absence of LMT/NOC/RTX strategic capital is conspicuous given the pivot narrative.

company_description: Develops co-packaged optics (CPO) — silicon photonic chiplets integrated directly with compute and switch ASICs to replace copper interconnects in AI data centers. Strategic investors include AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, and MediaTek; manufactures at TSMC and GlobalFoundries.
robotnik_take: Co-packaged optics is no longer speculative — AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, MediaTek all on the cap table is the clearest signal CPO is moving from R&D to production architecture for 2027-28 AI clusters. Public-market read-through: bearish for legacy pluggable optics names (Coherent COHR, Lumentum LITE), bullish for the silicon-photonics integration story at AVGO and MRVL. At 3.75B post-money, Ayar is priced as a strategic acquisition target as much as an independent — the customer list is essentially the buyer list.

company_description: Commercial space station developer building Haven-1, a single-module station launching to LEO, and Haven-2, a multi-module follow-on positioned as an ISS successor. Competing in NASA's Commercial LEO Destinations (CLD) program against Axiom Space, Sierra Space, and Blue Origin.
robotnik_take: First external round after Jed McCaleb's self-funded build — 300M equity + 200M debt, with QIA, IQT, Mitsui, Nikon signaling sovereign and strategic conviction. Comp set: Axiom Space, Sierra Space, Blue Origin Orbital Reef on the CLD competition; Vast is the most aggressive on timeline (Haven-1 launching 2026). The structural risk is that NASA CLD Phase 2 award concentration could leave the loser without ISS-transition revenue. Watch Haven-1 launch and PAM-6 mission as the binary catalysts.

company_description: Develops humanoid and cognitive robots equipped with onboard AI software for industrial and service applications. Flagship product is the 4NE1 humanoid, a 5.9-foot bipedal robot designed to understand natural-language instructions and handle payloads up to 220 pounds.
robotnik_take: Stablecoin issuer backing humanoid hardware is the cycle's strangest capital pairing — Tether's check alone is twice the prior largest single investment into a pure-play humanoid co. Comp set: Figure (2.6B+ private), Apptronik (5.5B post this batch), Galaxea AI (2.9B private). The German cap table is the clearest sovereignty signal in EU humanoid; matters more than the dollar amount. At ~€4B valuation, NEURA is now the European humanoid leader, full stop.

company_description: Spanish launch vehicle company developing MIURA 5, a small reusable launcher for European commercial and government missions. Mitsubishi Electric is a strategic investor anchoring Asian customer access.
robotnik_take: Mitsubishi Electric as strategic anchor matters more than the headline — a Japanese aerospace prime backing a Spanish small-launcher signals European sovereign-launch capacity is being plugged into Asian customer pull rather than just EU institutional demand. Closest public comp is Rocket Lab (RKLB) on small-lift cadence; ArianeGroup and Avio remain state-aligned competition in Europe. EIB tranche makes this a hybrid sovereignty-plus-strategic round. Bottleneck is MIURA 5 maiden flight execution.

company_description: US developer of critical mineral extraction and processing technologies. Competes with MP Materials and other rare earth processors in domestic supply-chain build-out.
robotnik_take: $11M seed with undisclosed lead is conspicuously thin for a US rare-earth/critical-minerals play in the current policy window — DPA Title III and DOE awards have lifted comparable rounds materially higher, and a quiet syndicate at this size signals technology risk rather than category enthusiasm. Comp set: MP Materials (MP) on US-listed rare-earth incumbent, Lynas (LYC AU) on ASX-listed processing, Energy Fuels (UUUU) on adjacent uranium-and-REE, USA Rare Earth as private peer. Pilot-plant validation is the binary milestone.

company_description: Operates AI-dedicated data centers and cloud GPU compute infrastructure across Europe, North America, and Asia. Vertically integrates GPU compute, networking, storage, and orchestration software for hyperscale AI training and inference customers.
robotnik_take: Largest European Series C on record at a 4x markup in six months — the European answer to the CoreWeave/Lambda neocloud trade, with the added strategic shimmer of Stargate UK/Norway. Comp set is CoreWeave (CRWV) public and Lambda private; the differentiator is sovereign-friendly siting, which is increasingly priced into UK and Nordic deployments. NVIDIA (NVDA) on the cap table is the load-bearing endorsement; valuation looks stretched if the IPO window narrows.

company_description: Designs high-radix networking silicon for AI data center infrastructure. Founded by ex-Broadcom and Marvell networking ASIC veterans (Drew Perkins and Omar Hassen); targets the same AI-networking problem as Enfabrica and Astera Labs from a different architectural angle.
co_investors: Matter Venture Partners, additional investors
robotnik_take: $200M Series A for a stealth-emerging networking-silicon startup only clears on founder pedigree — Drew Perkins and Omar Hassen have prior franchise-grade exits in optical and networking ASICs. Direct comp set: Enfabrica (private, $5B), Astera Labs (ALAB) on the public side; Broadcom (AVGO) Tomahawk and Nvidia (NVDA) Spectrum are the architectural counters. Doerr/Socratic anchoring without a hyperscaler strategic on the cap table is the soft spot — the AI-networking thesis works only if a Microsoft, Meta, or Google design win materializes in the next 18 months.

company_description: Develops cross-embodiment robot foundation models (FutureVision and DVA) using a video-pretraining approach — training on internet video rather than human teleoperation data. Targets robot OEMs and integrators needing generalist control models.
co_investors: Temasek, Mayfield Fund, Capricorn, additional investors
robotnik_take: Stealth-to-450M Series A at 1.7B is unusually large; Khosla + Temasek + Mayfield underwriting the video-pretraining thesis as an alternative to teleoperation-data approach used by Skild AI and Physical Intelligence. Strategic frame: if internet video generalizes to robot control, the data moat that Skild/PI have been building collapses. Valuation reasonable relative to PI ($11B at), but Rhoda is a generation behind in deployment evidence. Watch first cross-embodiment benchmarks.

company_description: Croatian manufacturer of FPV drones and smart goggles, expanding from consumer and drone-racing markets into defense FPV combat drones. Competes with DJI in consumer FPV and with emerging defense FPV vendors.
robotnik_take: Croatian FPV-and-goggles pivot from consumer drone-racing into NATO defense-FPV is the cleanest war-driven category transition in this window — Ukraine combat usage has validated FPV-drone economics at a scale Russian doctrine treats as transformative. Comp set: DJI on consumer FPV, Skydio on US autonomous, AeroVironment (AVAV) Switchblade on listed loitering munitions, Quantum Systems on EU dual-use. NATO procurement is the upside catalyst; lack of disclosed lead at $14M Series A is the conspicuous weakness.

company_description: Designs AI networking chips for data-center interconnect, targeting the high-radix switching demands of large AI training clusters. Competes with Broadcom and Marvell merchant networking silicon and NVIDIA's in-house networking division.
co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Altimeter Capital
robotnik_take: One of the largest pure-networking-silicon raises in the dataset — Lightspeed-led 500M Series B at 4.2B implies design wins already in hand. Comp set is direct and brutal: Broadcom (AVGO) Tomahawk/Jericho, Marvell (MRVL) Teralynx, NVIDIA (NVDA) Spectrum/Quantum, plus Astera Labs (ALAB) and Cisco (CSCO) Silicon One. AVGO is the franchise to beat in scale-out switching; Nexthop's bet is that hyperscaler custom-silicon trend extends to networking. Read-through is mildly bearish for AVGO networking moat if hyperscaler design wins materialize.

company_description: Builds industrial robots for factory automation, leveraging EV manufacturing IP from parent company Rivian. Founded by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe as a spinout focused on AI-powered manufacturing hardware.
robotnik_take: Rivian (RIVN) spinning out its manufacturing-automation IP as a separate venture under RJ Scaringe is the cleanest American example of EV-OEM-to-robotics adjacency, mirroring what Xpeng (XPEV) and Tesla (TSLA) have done internally. a16z and Accel co-leading at 2B Series A signals the bet is on EV manufacturing-process IP as the moat, not the robot design itself. Closest comp: Tesla Optimus (also EV-OEM-derived), Symbotic (SYM) on warehouse automation. Pre-commercial valuation is steep; depends on whether Rivian's manufacturing-process IP actually generalizes to third-party customers.

company_description: Builds household humanoid robots for consumer use, with the Memo dishwasher robot as its launch product. Competes in the emerging consumer-humanoid category alongside 1X (NEO) and The Bot Company.
robotnik_take: Coatue solo-leading at $1.15B for a consumer-humanoid pre-product is unusual sizing — the household humanoid category has been almost exclusively venture-funded until now, with crossover capital staying on the industrial side. Comp set: 1X (NEO consumer humanoid), The Bot Company (Cruise-founders), Figure on the industrial-first counter-positioning. Strategic frame is the consumer-vs-industrial humanoid bifurcation: Sunday bets consumer scales faster on demand pull, Figure and Apptronik bet industrial monetizes first.

company_description: Develops silicon photonic components — laser-based optical interconnects — for data center and telecom applications. Competes with Ayar Labs, Intel Silicon Photonics, and Cisco in integrated photonics.
co_investors: IAG Capital Partners, NVIDIA, additional existing investors
robotnik_take: NVIDIA (NVDA) participating in a silicon-photonics extension is the actual signal — even as Nvidia builds co-packaged optics in-house with Spectrum-X, it is hedging on the merchant-photonics layer through this stake. Comp set: Ayar Labs on optical I/O, Lightmatter on photonic compute, Marvell (MRVL) and Broadcom (AVGO) on CPO silicon; Coherent (COHR) and Lumentum (LITE) as merchant laser supply. Series A extension framing suggests Series B optionality, with Nvidia's stake providing the strategic underwrite.

company_description: UK Sheffield University spinout developing porous silicon anode material for next-generation lithium-ion batteries. Competes with Sila Nanotechnologies and Group14 on silicon-anode technology.
robotnik_take: Sheffield porous-silicon-anode preseed at $2.5M is early-R&D capital — academic spinout stage where the load-bearing question is whether scalable nanostructure synthesis works at cell-grade tolerances. Comp set: Sila Nanotechnologies and Group14 on US silicon-anode incumbents, Nexeon on UK porous-silicon peer, OneD Battery Sciences on silicon-nanowire coating; Shin-Etsu (4063 JP) and SUMCO (3436 JP) as the upstream silicon-feedstock listed peers. Pre-commercial; binary on first cell-maker qualification.

company_description: Japanese printed electronics company developing the SustainaCircuits additive circuit manufacturing process for flexible PCBs. Mitsubishi Electric is a strategic investor; competes with Unimicron and Ibiden in next-generation PCB manufacturing.
robotnik_take: Mitsubishi Electric anchoring a Japanese additive-PCB Series F is corporate strategic concentration risk — single-investor dependency at late stage usually telegraphs an acquisition path rather than independent commercial scale. Comp set: Unimicron (3037 TT) and Ibiden (4062 JP) on traditional PCB incumbents, AT&S (ATS AV) on Austrian-listed substrate, Nan Ya PCB (8046 TT) on Taiwanese peer. SustainaCircuits additive process targets the flexible-PCB segment; the underwriting case is automotive and EV-cabin electronics adoption.

DOE 500M across critical-minerals processing builds the demand floor that MP Materials (MP), Energy Fuels (UUUU), USA Rare Earth (USAR), and Lynas (LYC AU) need for project finance to clear. Strategic frame: sovereignty play paralleling DPA Title III rare-earth interventions. The structural problem the grant doesn't solve is offtake — without long-term commercial pricing commitments, processing capacity tends to be mothballed when Chinese export quotas loosen. Watch individual project awards for the actual signal.

company_description: Builds AI-powered industrial robots for heavy manufacturing applications. Sells robotic systems for high-physical-effort tasks; competes with FANUC, ABB, and Veo Robotics in the industrial-robotics segment.
co_investors: Jerry Yang, Gary Rieschel, Carnegie Mellon University
robotnik_take: YZi Labs (formerly Binance Labs) leading an industrial-robotics Series A is the most unusual capital-source pairing in the funding window — crypto-adjacent capital entering heavy-industry automation is either prescient or premature. Comp set: FANUC (6954 JP), ABB (ABBN SW), and KUKA (under Midea) on the incumbent side; Veo Robotics and Path Robotics on the US AI-powered industrial side. Industrial robotics has been mid-cycle weak; RoboForce's heavy-manufacturing focus is narrower than typical cobot pitches.

company_description: Designs AirJet, a solid-state active-cooling chip for laptops, smartphones, and increasingly servers. Replaces conventional fans with a silent piezoelectric cooler; relevant to thermal-envelope constraints on AI GPUs and high-power SoCs.
co_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, Mayfield Fund, Addition, Qualcomm Ventures, Alumni Ventures
robotnik_take: $143M Series D at $1.64B marks the first time thermal-management silicon has been priced as foundational AI infrastructure rather than a consumer-electronics niche. Qualcomm Ventures alongside Mayfield and Fidelity reads as design-win-driven — AirJet is moving from mobile/laptop demos into server/datacenter thermal envelopes where dollar TAM is an order of magnitude larger. Comp set: Vertiv (VRT) on liquid cooling, JetCool and ZutaCore on direct-to-chip. Bullish for the thermal-stack trade as GPU TDPs push past 1500W.

company_description: Israeli drone-swarm software company. Public on NASDAQ (SWMR) following a 2026 IPO; provides software for coordinating multi-drone defense operations.
robotnik_take: $15M NASDAQ micro-IPO for a drone-swarm software company is unusual — small defense-tech rarely lists at this scale, with most peers pursuing private growth rounds or SPACs. Comp set: Shield AI as private peer on autonomy, Anduril Lattice on coordination software, AeroVironment (AVAV) on listed defense-drone, Red Cat (RCAT) on the micro-cap defense-drone comparable. NASDAQ listing at $5/share, 3M shares creates a public-market read on swarm-software valuation — Swarmer becomes the only listed pure-play in coordination software.

company_description: German construction robotics company building the LIFTBOT material-transport robot that automates scaffold logistics and site material delivery. Targets construction sites with high labor turnover.
co_investors: Chevron Technology Ventures, Asahi Kasei, additional investors
robotnik_take: Chevron Technology Ventures and Asahi Kasei strategic participation tags KEWAZO as a chemical-and-energy industrial customer play — scaffold-logistics automation has direct payback on refinery turnarounds, where labor costs are highest. Comp set: Built Robotics on US construction autonomy, Hilti Group on the EU power-tool incumbent that would acquire, Dusty Robotics on layout-printing. Material-transport on construction sites is a real revenue category — Series A extension at $16M is modest but on-thesis for industrial-services automation.

company_description: Swiss ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab spinout building stair-climbing legged delivery robots for last-meter logistics. Acquired by Amazon in March 2026; formerly known as Swiss-Mile.
robotnik_take: Amazon acquiring an ETH Zurich legged-delivery spinout post-$22M seed is a textbook acqui-tech move — terms undisclosed but the strategic read is that Amazon is internalizing last-meter stair-climbing capability rather than partnering. Comp set: Agility Robotics (Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund stake) on bipedal logistics, Boston Dynamics under Hyundai (005380 KS) on legged platforms, ANYbotics on quadruped industrial, Unitree on China-cost legged peer. Amazon (AMZN) consolidating in-house robot-fleet IP is the strategic frame.

company_description: Chinese manufacturer of quadruped robots (Go2, B2) and humanoid robots (H1, G1), with humanoid products accounting for over half of revenue. Filed for a Shanghai STAR Market IPO in 2026.
robotnik_take: First quadruped/humanoid pure-play to file a public listing — sets the disclosure baseline for the entire sector. Revenue CNY 1.2B with humanoids already 51.5% of mix and CNY 105M net income makes this the only profitable humanoid name globally.
